title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
會試錄序
恭惟我
皇上至神極
聖應運紹
天御大紫之器握中黃之符
峻德豐功登邁三五四十一年以
來昭翼心於
===
上帝通馨治於神明周察吏政洞
燭民隱令發而化馳如霆心
懷而威動萬里肆今百司循
法羣黎樂生方內稱敉寧矣
然
皇上以吏治或壅於奸而含生之
物未盡浸潤於澤致治保民

燭民隱令發而化馳如霆心
懔而威動萬里肆令百司循

然
皇上以吏治或聖於奸而含生之
物未盡浸潤於澤致治保民
punctuated:
會試錄序

恭惟我皇上至神極聖，應運紹天，御大紫之器，握中黃之符，峻德豐功，登邁三五。四十一年以來，昭翼心於上帝，通馨治於神明，周察吏政，洞燭民隱。令發而化馳如霆，心懷而威動萬里。肆今百司循法，羣黎樂生，方內稱敉寧矣。然皇上以吏治或壅於奸，而含生之物未盡浸潤於澤，致治保民
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Metropolitan Examination

We reverently consider that our Emperor, supremely divine and utterly sagely, has responded to the destined course of events and succeeded to Heaven’s mandate. He commands the vessel of the Great Purple [?] and holds the tally of the Central Yellow [?]. His lofty virtue and abundant achievements surpass those of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors. For forty-one years, he has manifested his reverent heart before the Lord on High and made the fragrance of his governance reach the spirits. He scrutinizes the administration of officials comprehensively and clearly perceives the people’s hidden sufferings. When his commands issue, their transforming influence speeds like thunder; what he cherishes in his heart moves the realm ten thousand li away through his majestic power. Thus all offices now observe the laws, the common people delight in their livelihoods, and all within the realm is acclaimed as peaceful. Yet His Majesty considers that official administration may sometimes be obstructed by wickedness, and that living beings have not yet all been fully nourished by his beneficence; bringing about good government and protecting the people…

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
之圖
宸慮猶惓惓焉今歲壬戌為羣吏
述職之期又當會試天下士
上既命銓曹慎評庶位旌別其淑
慝茲復
命臣自
左右往典試事畀以罔羅英俊
===
===
之寄
聖意所嚮指視疇曩益加重矣臣
竊念章句賤流蒙
恩超擢置諸密勿即百其身無以
仰答
君父生成之德今者幸承
任使忻忭獨深竊謂可以藉手

之國
宸慮猶睠睠焉今歲壬戌爲羣吏
述職之期又當會試天下士

慝茲復

===

聖意所嚮指視疇曩益加重矣臣
竊念章句賤流蒙
恩超擢置諸密勿即百其身無以
仰答
君父生成之德今者幸承
任使忻忭獨深竊謂可以藉手
punctuated:
之圖，宸慮猶惓惓焉。今歲壬戌，為羣吏述職之期，又當會試天下士。上既命銓曹慎評庶位，旌別其淑慝，茲復命臣自左右往典試事，畀以罔羅英俊之寄。聖意所嚮指視疇曩益加重矣。
臣竊念章句賤流，蒙恩超擢，置諸密勿，即百其身，無以仰答君父生成之德。今者幸承任使，忻忭獨深，竊謂可以藉手
translation_en:
…His Majesty remains earnestly concerned with this undertaking. This year, renxu, is the appointed time for officials to report on their service, and also the occasion for the Metropolitan Examination of scholars from throughout the realm. His Majesty has already ordered the Ministry of Personnel to assess carefully the holders of all offices and distinguish the worthy from the wicked. Now he has further commanded me to leave his side and take charge of the examination, entrusting me with gathering outstanding talent. The importance attached to this charge in His Majesty’s intentions is greater still than in former times [?].
I humbly reflect that I am but a lowly student of textual phrases, yet through imperial grace I have been exceptionally promoted and placed in confidential service. Even with a hundred lives, I could not repay the nurturing benevolence of my sovereign and father. Now, fortunate to receive this commission, I feel especially profound joy, and humbly think that it may afford me a means…

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
圖効涓埃之報乃以是月辛
酉同諸執事詣
闕下辭臣復詣
迎和門叩首辭
皇上念臣直賛微勞
特頒金緋珎饈馳
賜棘院
===
天恩優異前此所未有也臣感激
非常之
眷敢不矢志思奮秉公竭忠務得
真材以少裨
聖化耶顧伏思之銓曹之課吏在
於黜不肖而校士之役在於
進賢二者事異而機同相須

闕下辭臣復詣
迎和門叩首辭
皇上念臣直贊微勞
特頒金緋珎饍
賜棘院
===
天恩優異前此所未有也臣感激
非常之
眷敢不矢志思奮秉公竭忠務得
真材以少裨
聖化耶顧伏思之銓曹之課吏在
於黜不肖而校士之役在於
進賢二者事異而機同相須
punctuated: 圖効涓埃之報，乃以是月辛酉，同諸執事詣闕下辭。臣復詣迎和門叩首辭，皇上念臣直賛微勞，特頒金緋、珎饈，馳賜棘院。天恩優異，前此所未有也。臣感激非常之眷，敢不矢志思奮，秉公竭忠，務得真材，以少裨聖化耶？顧伏思之，銓曹之課吏在於黜不肖，而校士之役在於進賢，二者事異而機同，相須
translation_en:
…to seek to repay even a tiny fraction of this favor. Thus, on the xinyou day of this month, I went with the other officials engaged in the examination to take leave at the palace. I then went again to Yinghe Gate, where I kowtowed and took leave. His Majesty, mindful of my modest labors in attendance and ceremonial assistance, specially bestowed gold insignia and scarlet robes, together with delicacies, dispatching them swiftly to the examination compound. This exceptional imperial favor was unprecedented. Moved by such extraordinary solicitude, how could I fail to resolve firmly to exert myself, uphold impartiality, devote my utmost loyalty, and strive to obtain men of genuine ability, thereby contributing a little to Your Majesty’s transforming influence?

Yet, reflecting humbly upon this, I consider that the personnel authorities’ assessment of officials consists in dismissing the unworthy, whereas the task of examining candidates consists in advancing the worthy. These two undertakings differ in their business but share the same underlying workings, each depending upon the other…

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
以成安民之治功也今觀其
所黜者或黷貨而貪或峻法
而刻或越度而縱或弱植而
靡是皆已業厥官計其三載
之政行昭晰而易見者也然
臣之所進則抱藝握鉛槧之
士如玉之在璞瑕瑜未呈欲
===
以三日之文而槩其人亦難
矣臣率諸同事者覃精凝思
披卷品隲至窮日夜之力雖
諸士之文雜然並陳于前而
純疵媺惡自章明較著粲然
而不能掩臣取而錄之言若
人人殊類皆抉微抒蘊標粹
alt_text:
以成安民之治功也今觀其
所黜者或黷貨而貪或峻法
而刻或越度而縱或弱植而
靡是皆已業厥官計其三載
之政行昭晰而易見者也然
臣之所進則抱藝握鉛槧之
士如玉之在璞瑕瑜未呈欲
以三日之文而槩其人亦難
===
矣臣率諸同事者覃精凝思
披卷品隲至竆日夜之力雖
諸士之文雜然並陳于前而
純疵孅惡自章明較著粲然
而不能掩臣取而錄之言若
人人殊類皆抉微抒藴標粹
punctuated: 以成安民之治功也。今觀其所黜者，或黷貨而貪，或峻法而刻，或越度而縱，或弱植而靡，是皆已業厥官，計其三載之政行，昭晰而易見者也。然臣之所進，則抱藝握鉛槧之士，如玉之在璞，瑕瑜未呈，欲以三日之文而槩其人，亦難矣。臣率諸同事者，覃精凝思，披卷品隲，至窮日夜之力。雖諸士之文雜然並陳于前，而純疵媺惡，自章明較著，粲然而不能掩。臣取而錄之，言若人人殊類，皆抉微抒蘊，標粹
translation_en:
…to accomplish the work of governing that brings peace to the people. Now, among those dismissed, some are greedy, tainted by the pursuit of wealth; some are harsh, applying the law with excessive severity; some are unrestrained, exceeding proper bounds; and some are weak in resolve and pliant. All these men have already served in office: when their conduct in government over three years is assessed, it is clear and readily discernible. Yet those whom your servant advances are scholars possessed of literary learning, wielding writing leads and tablets. They are like jade still within its rough matrix, its flaws and virtues not yet revealed. To judge the whole person from three days’ writing is indeed difficult.

Your servant led his fellow examiners in concentrating their minds and deliberating deeply, opening the scripts and appraising them, exhausting their strength by day and night. Although the candidates’ writings lay before us in a bewildering array, their purity and flaws, merits and defects, became clear and distinct, plainly visible and impossible to conceal. Your servant selected and recorded them. Although their expression seemed to differ from person to person, all brought subtle meanings to light, gave voice to what lay within, and set forth the essence…

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
揆奇各以其素所蓄者發之
文有莊嚴瑩徹其詞峻以潔
者曰是能剖析義利士之廉
而不劌者也有溫醇爾雅其
詞和以平者曰是能涵養德
性士之愷悌而不苟者也有
詞之縝密典則從容於法度
===
之中者是必履正奉公之士
知其不淪於縱也有詞之雄
深閎肆發舒其剛大之氣者
是必任重致遠之士知其不
流于靡也夫文者德之華也
言者心之聲也緣華以稽其
德因聲以遡其心錄其先資

性士之愷悌而不苛者也有
詞之縝密典則從容於法度
===
之中者是必履正奉公之士
知其不淪於縱也有詞之雄
深閎肆發舒其剛大之氣者
是必任重致遠之士知其不
流于靡也夫文者德之華也
言者心之聲也緣華以稽其
德因聲以遡其心錄其先資
punctuated: 揆奇，各以其素所蓄者發之。文有莊嚴瑩徹，其詞峻以潔者，曰：「是能剖析義利，士之廉而不劌者也。」有溫醇爾雅，其詞和以平者，曰：「是能涵養德性，士之愷悌而不苟者也。」有詞之縝密典則，從容於法度之中者，是必履正奉公之士，知其不淪於縱也。有詞之雄深閎肆，發舒其剛大之氣者，是必任重致遠之士，知其不流于靡也。夫文者，德之華也；言者，心之聲也。緣華以稽其德，因聲以遡其心，錄其先資
translation_en: …and bringing forth the extraordinary, each expressing what he had long cultivated within himself. Where a composition is dignified and lucid, its language elevated and pure, I say: “This man can distinguish moral rightness from personal profit; he is a scholar of integrity whose sharp edges do not cut.” Where a composition is warm, mellow, and refined, its language harmonious and balanced, I say: “This man can nurture his moral nature; he is a kindly and approachable scholar who is never careless.” Where the language is meticulous and conforms to classical standards, moving with ease within established rules, its author must be a scholar who walks uprightly and serves the public good; we know that he will not lapse into self-indulgence. Where the language is powerful, profound, expansive, and unrestrained, giving expression to his firm and ample vital force, its author must be a scholar capable of bearing heavy responsibilities and reaching distant goals; we know that he will not lapse into weakness. Now, writing is the flowering of virtue, and words are the voice of the heart. Through the flower we examine his virtue; through the voice we trace his heart. I record their prior attainments [?]…

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
之言而獻之於
上自此而敷對
大廷陳布有位諸士因言以成
其信内之亮工熙載外之展
采錯事乂安黎元翌賛
鴻化以副
當宁致治保民之懷則今日所進
===
庶可逭他日之黜矣臣又聞
之一年之計樹穀十年之計
樹木百年之計樹人夫良農
之樹穀必擇嘉種焉以裕饗
神粒民之資也若稊稗稂莠
則芟夷蘊崇之矣場師之樹
木必掄美材焉以需清廟明
alt_text:
之言而獻之於
上自此而敷對
大廷陳布有位諸士因言以成
其信內之亮工熙載外之展
寀錯事乂安黎元翼贊
鴻化以副
當宁致治保民之懷則今日所進
===
庶可遒他日之黜矣臣又聞
之一年之計樹穀十年之計
樹木百年之計樹人夫良農
之樹穀必擇嘉種焉以裕饗
神粒民之資也若莠稗稂莠
則芟夷蘊崇之矣場師之樹
木必掄美材焉以需清廟明
punctuated:
之言而獻之於上。自此而敷對大廷，陳布有位，諸士因言以成其信，内之亮工熙載，外之展采錯事，乂安黎元，翌賛鴻化，以副當宁致治保民之懷，則今日所進，庶可逭他日之黜矣。
臣又聞之：「一年之計，樹穀；十年之計，樹木；百年之計，樹人。」夫良農之樹穀，必擇嘉種焉，以裕饗神粒民之資也。若稊稗稂莠，則芟夷蘊崇之矣。場師之樹木，必掄美材焉，以需清廟明
translation_en:
…their words and present them to His Majesty. From this point onward, they will respond before the great court and be appointed to official posts. By their deeds, these gentlemen will establish the trustworthiness of their words: within the court, they will assist in its work and bring its undertakings to fruition; outside it, they will exercise their abilities and arrange affairs. They will bring peace and order to the common people and assist the great transforming influence of imperial rule, fulfilling the reigning sovereign’s desire to secure good government and protect the people. Thus, those advanced today may perhaps escape dismissal in days to come.
Your servant has also heard it said: “For a plan of one year, plant grain; for a plan of ten years, plant trees; for a plan of a hundred years, cultivate people.” When a good farmer plants grain, he invariably selects fine seed, thereby ensuring abundant supplies for offerings to the spirits and food for the people. As for tares, barnyard grass, and other weeds, he cuts them down, uproots them, and gathers them into heaps. When a gardener plants trees, he invariably selects those that will yield fine timber, to meet the needs of the Clear Temple and the Bright …

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
堂之用也若荆榛棫棘則剪
伐攘剔之矣我
祖宗豐芑之仁
皇上菁莪棫樸之化長養培植以
樹多士既深且久乃今錄於
有司若嘉種之升豆登美材
之中繩墨也誠能懷感
===
國恩爭自磨濯策鉅偉之績建
駿奕之功以養萬民以楨邦
國為
宗社樹億萬禩靈長之計則多
士厚於自樹而臣亦慶於得
人庶可以對揚
恩命之萬一矣其或行弗逮言文
alt_text:
堂之用也若剃荆榛櫛棘則剪
伐擴剔之矣我
祖宗豐芑之仁
皇上菁莪棫樸之化長養培植以
樹多士既深且久乃今錄於
有司若嘉種之升豆登美材
之中繩墨也誠能懷感
國恩爭自磨濯策鉅偉之績建
駿奕之功以養萬民以楨邦
===
國爲
宗社樹億萬禩靈長之計則多
士厚於自樹而臣亦庶於得
人庶可以對揚
恩命之萬一矣其或行弗逮言文
punctuated: 堂之用也；若荆榛棫棘，則剪伐攘剔之矣。我祖宗豐芑之仁，皇上菁莪棫樸之化，長養培植，以樹多士，既深且久。乃今錄於有司，若嘉種之升豆登、美材之中繩墨也。誠能懷感國恩，爭自磨濯，策鉅偉之績，建駿奕之功，以養萬民，以楨邦國，為宗社樹億萬禩靈長之計，則多士厚於自樹，而臣亦慶於得人，庶可以對揚恩命之萬一矣。其或行弗逮言，文
translation_en: …for use in the hall; as for brambles, hazel, scrub oaks, and thorns, these are cut down and cleared away. Our imperial ancestors’ benevolence, likened to luxuriant millet, and His Majesty’s transforming influence, likened to flourishing mugwort and oak shrubs, have nurtured and cultivated the many scholars with profound care over a long period. Now selected by the responsible officials, they are like fine grain placed in ritual vessels [?], or excellent timber that conforms to the carpenter’s line. If they can truly cherish gratitude for the state’s beneficence, vie in refining and cleansing themselves, accomplish great achievements, and establish magnificent deeds, thereby sustaining the myriad people, serving as pillars of the state, and laying plans for the enduring prosperity of the ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain through countless ages, then these scholars will have firmly established themselves, and I, your servant, will also rejoice in having obtained worthy men. Thus I might requite and proclaim even a ten-thousandth part of the gracious charge entrusted to me. Should their conduct, however, fall short of their words, and their writing …

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
不適用始以賢進而終以不
肖黜是自捐其嘉而斲其所
以為美也庸不負
國家樹人之盛心哉是舉也
上允禮部之請以臣煒偕學士臣
份為考試官而同考試則右
諭德臣汝楫侍讀臣鏜孫修
撰臣士美編修臣旻臣希烈
臣汝嘉臣四維臣弘謨檢討
臣可行臣泰臣自強都給事
中臣夢龍臣岳臣益署郎中
臣承勳臣汝驥主事臣一道
知貢舉則尚書臣訥侍郎臣
拱監試則御史臣承華臣復

以爲美也庸不負
國家樹人之盛心哉是舉也
上允禮部之請以臣煒偕學士臣
份爲考試官而同考試則右
諭德臣汝楫侍讀臣鏜孫修
撰臣士美編修臣旻臣希烈
===
臣汝嘉臣四維臣弘謨檢討
臣可行臣泰臣自強都給事
中臣夢龍臣岳臣益署郎中
臣承業臣汝讜主事臣一道
知貢舉則尚書臣訥侍郎臣
拱監試則御史臣承華臣復
punctuated:
不適用，始以賢進，而終以不肖黜，是自捐其嘉，而斲其所以為美也。庸不負國家樹人之盛心哉？

是舉也，上允禮部之請，以臣煒偕學士臣份為考試官。而同考試則右諭德臣汝楫，侍讀臣鏜孫，修撰臣士美，編修臣旻、臣希烈、臣汝嘉、臣四維、臣弘謨，檢討臣可行、臣泰、臣自強，都給事中臣夢龍、臣岳、臣益，署郎中臣承勳、臣汝驥，主事臣一道。知貢舉則尚書臣訥、侍郎臣拱；監試則御史臣承華、臣復。
translation_en:
…is unsuited to practical use, and they advance initially as worthy men but are ultimately dismissed as unworthy, they themselves will have cast away their excellence and hewn away that which made them admirable. Would this not betray the state's earnest intention to cultivate men of talent?

For this examination, His Majesty approved the Ministry of Rites' request and appointed your servant Wei, together with Academician Fen, as Examiners. The Associate Examiners were your servants R uji [Ruji], Right Mentor; Tangsun [?], Reader-in-Waiting; Shimei, Senior Compiler; Min, Xilie, Rujia, Siwei, and Hongmo, Junior Compilers; Kexing, Tai, and Ziqiang, Examining Editors; Menglong, Yue, and Yi, Chief Supervising Secretaries; Chengxun and Ruji, Acting Bureau Directors; and Yidao, Secretary. Your servants Ne, Minister, and Gong, Vice Minister, administered the examination. Your servants Chenghua and Fu, Investigating Censors, monitored the examination.

獻焉

translation_en:
More than four thousand five hundred candidates sat the examination. Following established practice, they were examined in three sessions. In accordance with the imperial decision, three hundred outstanding candidates were selected. Twenty of their finest compositions were printed and compiled into a record for presentation to the throne.
This preface was respectfully composed by Yuan Wei, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Revenue, and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall.

translation_en:
Metropolitan Examination of the Forty-first Year of Jiajing (1562)

Officials in Charge of the Examination:
Yan Na, Minister of Rites concurrently serving as Academician of the Hanlin Academy, had the courtesy name Minqing. Registered in Changshu County, Zhili, and a native of Wu County, he became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the xinchou year (1541).
Gao Gong, Grand Master for Excellent Counsel and Left Vice Minister of Rites, had the courtesy name Suqing. A native of Xinzheng County, Henan, he became a metropolitan graduate in the xinchou year (1541).

Examiners:
Yuan Wei, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Revenue concurrently serving as Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall, had the courtesy name Maozhong. A native of Cixi County, Zhejiang, he became a metropolitan graduate in the wuxu year (1538).
Dong Fen, Grand Master for Excellent Counsel and Left Vice Minister of Personnel concurrently serving as Academician of the Hanlin Academy and administering the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent, had the courtesy name Yongjun. A native of Wucheng County, Zhejiang, he became a metropolitan graduate in the xinchou year (1541).

Associate Examiners:
Tang Ruji, Grand Master for Exemplary Instruction and Right Mentor of the Right Secretariat of the Heir Apparent, had the courtesy name Siji. A native of Lanxi County, Zhejiang, he became a metropolitan graduate in the gengxu year (1550).
Wang Tang, Expositor-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy, had the courtesy name Zhenzong. A native of Yin County, Zhejiang, he became a metropolitan graduate in the dingwei year (1547).
Ding Shimei, Senior Compiler of the Hanlin Academy and Gentleman for Undertaking Service, had the courtesy name Bangyan. A native of Qinghe County, Zhili, he became a metropolitan graduate in the jiwei year (1559).
Lü Min, Junior Compiler of the Hanlin Academy and Gentleman of the Forest of Literature, had the courtesy name Renfu. A native of Longxi County, Fujian, he became a metropolitan graduate in the guichou year (1553).
Wang Xilie, Junior Compiler of the Hanlin Academy and Gentleman of the Forest of Literature, had the courtesy name Zizhong. Registered in Nanchang County, Jiangxi, and a native of Linchuan County, he became a metropolitan graduate in the guichou year (1553).
Hu Rujia, Junior Compiler of the Hanlin Academy and Gentleman for Rendering Service, had the courtesy name Maoli. From Yingyang Guard in Nanjing, he became a metropolitan graduate in the guichou year (1553).
Zhang Siwei, Junior Compiler of the Hanlin Academy and Gentleman of the Forest of Literature, had the courtesy name Ziwei. A native of Puzhou, Shanxi, he became a metropolitan graduate in the guichou year (1553).
Yao Hongmo, Junior Compiler of the Hanlin Academy and Gentleman of the Forest of Literature, had the courtesy name Jiwen. A native of Xiushui County, Zhejiang, he became a metropolitan graduate in the guichou year (1553).
Wu Kexing, Examining Editor of the Hanlin Academy and Gentleman for Meritorious Service, had the courtesy name Ziyan. Registered in Wujin County, Zhili, and a native of Yixing County, he became a metropolitan graduate in the guichou year (1553).
Lu Tai, Examining Editor of the Hanlin Academy and Gentleman for Meritorious Service, had the courtesy name Weixiu. A native of Yin County, Zhejiang, he became a metropolitan graduate in the guichou year (1553).

Ma Ziqiang, Reviewer in the Hanlin Academy, held the rank of Gentleman for Attendant Service. His courtesy name was Tiqian; he was from Tongzhou, Shaanxi, and became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in 1553 (guichou).

Liang Menglong was Chief Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel. His courtesy name was Qianji; he was from Zhending County, Zhili, and became a metropolitan graduate in 1553 (guichou).

Qiu Yue was Chief Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Rites. His courtesy name was Zizhan; he was from Huanggang County, Huguang, and became a metropolitan graduate in 1547 (dingwei).

Zhang Yi, Chief Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for War, held the rank of Gentleman for Rendering Service. His courtesy name was Shunqing; he was from Fengcheng County, Jiangxi, and became a metropolitan graduate in 1550 (gengxu).

Wu Chengtao, Principal Secretary acting as Director of the Bureau of Evaluations in the Ministry of Personnel, held the rank of Gentleman for Meritorious Virtue. His courtesy name was Renfu; he was from Wujiang County, Zhili, and became a metropolitan graduate in 1553 (guichou).

Xu Ruji, Principal Secretary acting as Director of the Bureau of Equipment in the Ministry of War, held the rank of Gentleman for Meritorious Virtue. His courtesy name was Deqing; he was from Ningguo County, Zhili, and became a metropolitan graduate in 1553 (guichou).

Luo Yidao, Principal Secretary of the Shanxi Bureau in the Ministry of Justice, held the rank of Gentleman for Meritorious Virtue. His courtesy name was Guanqing; he was from Dongguan County, Guangdong, and became a metropolitan graduate in 1550 (gengxu).

Examination Monitoring Officials:

Li Chenghua, Investigating Censor for the Zhejiang Circuit, held the rank of Gentleman of Literature. His courtesy name was Shifu; he was from Quwo County, Shanxi, and became a metropolitan graduate in 1547 (dingwei).

Luo Fu, Investigating Censor for the Fujian Circuit, held the rank of Gentleman for Rendering Service. His courtesy name was Zizhen; he was from Nanchang County, Jiangxi, and became a metropolitan graduate in 1553 (guichou).

Proctors:

Lao Kan, Principal Secretary of the Bureau of Ceremonies in the Ministry of Rites, held the rank of Gentleman for Upright Service. His courtesy name was Junren; he was from Dehua County, Jiangxi, and became a metropolitan graduate in 1556 (bingchen).

Chai Lai, Principal Secretary of the Bureau of Receptions in the Ministry of Rites, held the rank of Gentleman for Upright Service. His courtesy name was Jidong; he was registered in Shuntian Prefecture and was a native of Yin County, Zhejiang. He became a metropolitan graduate in 1556 (bingchen).

Officials Responsible for Printing Examination Papers:

punctuated:
第壹場

四書

事君，能致其身。

悠久無疆。

文王以民力為臺為沼，而民歡樂之，謂其臺曰靈臺，謂其沼曰靈沼。

易

天且弗違，而況於人乎？

元吉在上，大成也。

非天下之至神，其孰能與於此？

天地設位，聖人成能。

書

光被四表，格于上下。

江漢朝宗于海。

曰雨，曰暘，曰燠，曰寒，曰風，曰時。五者來備，各以其敘。

道洽政治，澤潤生民。

詩
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

In serving his ruler, he can devote himself utterly.

Enduring forever, without limit.

King Wen used the people's labor to build a terrace and a pond, yet the people delighted in this. They called his terrace the Spirit Terrace and his pond the Spirit Pond.

Book of Changes

Even Heaven does not oppose him; how much less would human beings?

Supreme good fortune in the upper position signifies great accomplishment.

Were it not the most spiritually wondrous thing under Heaven, what could participate in this?

Heaven and Earth establish their positions; the sage brings their capacities to fulfillment.

Book of Documents

His radiance extended to the four extremities and reached above and below.

The Jiang and Han rivers flow toward the sea, as lords attend court to pay homage to their sovereign.

These are rain, sunshine, warmth, cold, and wind, and their timeliness. These five come in full measure, each in its proper sequence.

The Way prevailed and government was well ordered; beneficence nourished the people.

Book of Odes

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:

似續妣祖築室百堵西南其戸爰居爰處
爰笑爰語
顯顯令德宜民宜人受祿于天
以介眉壽永言保之思皇多祜
春秋
春正月公會宋公蔡侯衛侯于曹夏四
月公會宋公衛侯陳侯蔡侯伐鄭桓公
十有六年
===
夏單伯會伐宋莊公十有四年齊師宋師
曹師城邢僖公元年
公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊世子光莒子
邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭會于
蕭魚襄公十有一年甲午衛侯衎復歸
于衛襄公二十有六年
叔孫舍至自晉昭公二十有四年
禮記

===

曹師城邢〔僖公元年〕
公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊世子光莒子
邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭會于
蕭魚〔襄公十有一年〕甲午衛侯衎復歸
于衛〔襄公二十有六年〕
叔孫舍至自晉〔昭公二十有四年〕
禮記
君賜車馬乘以拜賜衣服服以拜賜
punctuated:
于以盛之？維筐及筥。于以湘之？維錡及釡。
似續妣祖，築室百堵，西南其戸，爰居爰處，爰笑爰語。
顯顯令德，宜民宜人，受祿于天。
以介眉壽，永言保之，思皇多祜。

春秋
春正月，公會宋公、蔡侯、衛侯于曹。夏四月，公會宋公、衛侯、陳侯、蔡侯伐鄭。桓公十有六年。
夏，單伯會伐宋。莊公十有四年。齊師、宋師、曹師城邢。僖公元年。
公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，會于蕭魚。襄公十有一年。甲午，衛侯衎復歸于衛。襄公二十有六年。
叔孫舍至自晉。昭公二十有四年。

禮記
君賜車馬，乘以拜；賜衣服，服以拜賜。
translation_en:
In what shall we put them? In square and round bamboo baskets. In what shall we cook them? In cauldrons with legs and cauldrons without legs.

Continuing the legacy of their foremothers and forefathers, they build a house with a hundred sections of wall, its doors facing west and south. Here they dwell and settle; here they laugh and converse.

Resplendent is your excellent virtue, bringing benefit to the people and to others; you receive blessings from Heaven.

Thereby attain venerable longevity; preserve it forever. Great indeed are the many blessings.

Spring and Autumn Annals

In spring, in the first month, the duke met with the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, and the Marquis of Wei at Cao. In summer, in the fourth month, the duke joined the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Marquis of Chen, and the Marquis of Cai in attacking Zheng. The sixteenth year of Duke Huan.

In summer, the Earl of Shan joined the attack on Song. The fourteenth year of Duke Zhuang. The armies of Qi, Song, and Cao built walls at Xing. The first year of Duke Xi.

The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu in attacking Zheng; they met at Xiaoyu. The eleventh year of Duke Xiang. On the jiawu day, Kan, Marquis of Wei, returned again to Wei. The twenty-sixth year of Duke Xiang.

Shusun She arrived back from Jin. The twenty-fourth year of Duke Zhao.

Book of Rites

When the ruler bestows a carriage and horses, one rides in the carriage to make obeisance in thanks; when he bestows clothing, one wears it to make obeisance in thanks for the gift.

Requisitioning military supplies in frontier regions.
Weaving prohibited varieties of silk fabric.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: When the emperors and kings of antiquity established magnificent virtue, there were necessarily ministers of outstanding literary talent to praise it and record it; only then was that magnificent virtue made manifest. For the age of Tang and Yu, this can be examined in the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents. From the Han onward, literary ministers extolled virtue and celebrated achievements, proclaiming their sovereigns’ excellence. Historical accounts amply attest to this, as with Sima Xiangru and Ban Gu under the Han, and Zhang Yue and Liu Zongyuan under the Tang. Yet Shao Yong of the Song, in discussing government, said: “Our dynasty has five achievements unprecedented since the age of Tang and Yu.” Yong was a great Confucian scholar of his age, and his judgment surely had a basis. Why not investigate closely what he meant?

We reverently reflect upon our Emperor Taizu Gao, endowed by Heaven with sagely and divine qualities, who founded the realm of China. His lofty virtue and towering achievements cannot be exhaustively recounted. Literary courtiers of recent times have likewise said: “Our dynasty, too, has five achievements in which it surpasses all preceding dynasties.” Might they have been inspired by Yong to single out its most far-reaching and momentous achievements? Early in our dynasty, a Confucian minister, in a preface to the Daily Record of the Great Ming, once invoked six matters in a comparison with Tang [?]…

translation_en:
…the achievements of the sagely ancestor. I wonder whether the arguments of these two ministers, one earlier and one later, tally with each other. Now, [illegible character], examining what they enumerated, these truly surpass those of all former kings and stand unrivaled in splendor. How could the affairs of the Song be spoken of in the same breath? Yet the particulars of his sagely government that transcend past and present are not limited to these. Can you enumerate them all?

When Emperor Wen, Chengzu, pacified internal disorders and secured the foundations, he bequeathed peace to the ancestral temples and the altars of state for countless ages. His achievement differed in no respect from the sagely ancestor’s work of ordering Heaven and Earth. Coming to our present Emperor, his Way flourishes in carrying forward his predecessors’ undertakings, and his reign brings a restoration. He promulgates the August Norm to bestow blessings upon the common people, discerns how things converge and interconnect, and implements the established rites. His government and transforming influence rise resplendent and extend throughout the universe, thereby displaying [?] Taizu’s brilliant radiance and exalting Chengzu’s great accomplishments. He stands far above the emperors and kings of antiquity; the Han, Tang, and Song dare not aspire to match him. Can you set forth and extol these achievements?

The sagely ancestor and his divine descendant, illustrious and luminous, have achieved a government unequaled through a hundred generations. Surely there must be a foundation upon which they accomplished this. Can you also describe its broad outlines? Today, all who are eloquent and all who wield the writing brush wish to exhaust their literary inspiration in offering songs of praise. You candidates surely…

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
人也幸為我詳著之
問博物洽聞儒者格致之學也昔人謂大
人之胷懷非一才高智大故於百家之
言無所不包則遊神玄覽信君子所貴
也試舉數事與諸士析之春秋之世列
國多良大夫有著牧民山高乘馬輕重
九府之篇有讀三墳五典八索九丘之
書可得而陳之歟有因出使鄰國而識
實沈臺駘之祟有因龍見絳郊而為畜
===
龍御龍之說又可得而僂指歟孔子大
聖人也黨人稱之為博學太宰訝之為
多能夫六經所刪述炳如日星天下誦
習而講靡之無論已然嘗解商羊之舞
剖萍實之徵悟羵羊之祕決陳人庭隼
之疑對越人執骨之問夫此五者非耳
目所濡染何以能旁通之若是也豈天
縱聰明之盡者自無所不知歟抑亦有
所考歟至漢人雖誦法孔子其智識之

punctuated:
人也，幸為我詳著之。

問：博物洽聞，儒者格致之學也。昔人謂大人之胷懷非一，才高智大，故於百家之言無所不包，則遊神玄覽，信君子所貴也。試舉數事與諸士析之。春秋之世，列國多良大夫，有著《牧民》《山高》《乘馬》《輕重》《九府》之篇，有讀《三墳》《五典》《八索》《九丘》之書，可得而陳之歟？有因出使鄰國而識實沈、臺駘之祟，有因龍見絳郊而為畜龍、御龍之說，又可得而僂指歟？孔子，大聖人也。黨人稱之為博學，太宰訝之為多能。夫六經所刪述，炳如日星，天下誦習而講靡之，無論已。然嘗解商羊之舞，剖萍實之徵，悟羵羊之祕，決陳人庭隼之疑，對越人執骨之問。夫此五者，非耳目所濡染，何以能旁通之若是也？豈天縱聰明之盡者，自無所不知歟？抑亦有所考歟？至漢人，雖誦法孔子，其智識之
translation_en:
…are such men. Kindly set this out in detail for me.

Question: Broad knowledge of things and extensive learning constitute the Confucian scholar’s study of investigating things and extending knowledge. A man of old said that great men’s minds are not confined to one sphere, their talents being lofty and their wisdom vast [?]; thus they encompass the teachings of all the schools. Surely, then, letting the mind roam and contemplating profound mysteries are things the gentleman esteems. Let us raise several matters for you candidates to analyze.

During the Spring and Autumn period, the various states had many worthy grand masters. One wrote the chapters “Governing the People,” “Mountain Heights” [?], “Riding Horses,” “The Light and the Heavy,” and “The Nine Treasuries”; another read the books Three Tombs, Five Canons, Eight Cords, and Nine Mounds. Can you give an account of them? One, while serving as an envoy to a neighboring state, recognized the baleful influence of Shichen and Tai Tai; another, when a dragon appeared outside Jiang, expounded on dragon rearing and dragon driving. Can you enumerate these instances as well?

Confucius was a great sage. A man of Daxiang praised him for his broad learning, and the Grand Steward marveled at his many abilities. What he edited and transmitted in the Six Classics shines like the sun and stars; all under Heaven recite, study, and expound upon it [?]. We need not discuss that further. Yet he also explained the dance of the shangyang bird, elucidated the portent of the duckweed fruit, understood the mystery of the fen sheep, resolved the doubts concerning the falcon in a courtyard in Chen, and answered the question about the men of Yue bearing a bone. If these five things were not matters to which his eyes and ears had been exposed, how could he have understood them so comprehensively? Could it be that someone endowed by Heaven with intelligence in its fullest measure naturally knows everything? Or did he also have sources to consult? As for the men of Han, although they recited Confucius’s teachings and took him as their model, their knowledge and understanding…

text:
相越何啻百倍然亦有辨騶牙之出□
有達重常之竒者有究貳負之詭者有
別豹鼠之異者漢以後又有能察劔氣
者有能曉角端者數子之見亦通朗矣
不識與孔子之多能可庶幾否歟孔門
稱好學而傳博文之教者顏子一人而
已今考其遺書曰潜心曰如愚而所博
之學不少概見豈孔子有所隱而不盡
傳之歟或資雖近道而學不博綜將出
===
春秋數子之下即漢晉人亦弗若歟抑
其所博者自有在也諸生彊學待問有
年矣願以前所詢者攄蘊以對
問士君子之窮經術所以經世也試以今
天下所最切而可慮者商之夫天生五
穀以資生也其生五金以待用也皆本
之五行以運布於天下五行未嘗有闕
而說者乃謂金無餘氣豈金或有所闕
而世之金遂亦因之歟然五穀木屬也

相越何啻百倍！然亦有辨騶牙之出□，有達重常之竒者，有究貳負之詭者，有別豹鼠之異者。漢以後，又有能察劔氣者，有能曉角端者。數子之見亦通朗矣，不識與孔子之多能可庶幾否歟？孔門稱好學而傳博文之教者，顏子一人而已。今考其遺書，曰潜心，曰如愚，而所博之學不少概見。豈孔子有所隱而不盡傳之歟？或資雖近道，而學不博綜，將出春秋數子之下，即漢晉人亦弗若歟？抑其所博者自有在也？諸生彊學待問有年矣，願以前所詢者攄蘊以對。
問：士君子之窮經術，所以經世也。試以今天下所最切而可慮者商之。夫天生五穀以資生也，其生五金以待用也，皆本之五行以運布於天下。五行未嘗有闕，而說者乃謂金無餘氣，豈金或有所闕，而世之金遂亦因之歟？然五穀木屬也，
translation_en:
…the disparity between them was surely more than a hundredfold! Yet there were also those who could identify the appearance of the zouya beast [the following character is illegible], those who understood the marvel of Chongchang [?], those who investigated the strange affair of Erfu, and those who distinguished the peculiarities of the leopard-mouse [?]. After the Han, too, there were those who could discern the emanations of swords and those who could recognize the jueduan beast. These men’s understanding was also comprehensive and clear. I wonder whether they could approach Confucius in his many abilities. Among Confucius’s disciples, Master Yan alone was praised as devoted to learning and received the teaching of broad learning in cultural writings. Yet when we examine the surviving writings concerning him, they speak of his immersing his mind in study and of his seeming foolish; scarcely any indication appears of the breadth of his learning. Did Confucius conceal something and fail to transmit it fully? Or, though Master Yan’s natural endowment was close to the Way, was his learning insufficiently broad and comprehensive, placing him below those men of the Spring and Autumn period, and even below men of the Han and Jin? Or did the breadth of his learning lie elsewhere? You candidates have studied diligently for years in preparation for such questions. I hope you will unfold your accumulated understanding in reply to the inquiries above.
Question: The purpose for which gentlemen thoroughly investigate classical learning is to bring order to the world. Let us consider this in relation to the most pressing and troubling concerns in the realm today. Heaven produces the five grains to sustain life and the five metals to meet practical needs. All are rooted in the Five Phases, whose operation distributes them throughout the world. The Five Phases have never lacked any constituent, yet commentators say that Metal has no surplus vital energy. Could there be some deficiency in Metal, with the metals of the world consequently affected by it? Yet the five grains belong to Wood…

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
又何以有不足歟昔人有言明君貴五
穀而賤金玉又云天地生財不在官則
在民是五穀與金賤貴相低昂也其在
官在民勢亦相為盈虛也顧今之時歲
有豐歉穀既不常盈宜金或有餘矣而
亦往往告匱將何所重而後可歟天下
方多事府庫不充司國計者至為一切
補救之術亦尚未充也而閭閻困詘又
輒稱曰民力盡矣豈在官在民之說不
===
足信歟頃者
皇上軫念農事加意國儲每春和即下
詔勸耕一遇水旱輒竭虔祈禱覈供億慎予
賚雖
上用之所須猶數稽裁之計歲所省不下數十
萬所謂豐源節流之道至矣而奉行
德意則在有司意者有所未至歟夫興一利不
若除一害藏富於國不若藏富於民茲
欲去其害穀與金者俾上與下兩利而

punctuated: 又何以有不足歟？昔人有言：「明君貴五穀而賤金玉。」又云：「天地生財，不在官則在民。」是五穀與金賤貴相低昂也，其在官在民，勢亦相為盈虛也。顧今之時，歲有豐歉，穀既不常盈，宜金或有餘矣，而亦往往告匱，將何所重而後可歟？天下方多事，府庫不充，司國計者至為一切補救之術，亦尚未充也。而閭閻困詘，又輒稱曰：「民力盡矣。」豈在官在民之說不足信歟？頃者，皇上軫念農事，加意國儲，每春和即下詔勸耕，一遇水旱輒竭虔祈禱，覈供億，慎予賚，雖上用之所須，猶數稽裁之，計歲所省不下數十萬。所謂豐源節流之道至矣，而奉行德意則在有司，意者有所未至歟？夫興一利不若除一害，藏富於國不若藏富於民。茲欲去其害穀與金者，俾上與下兩利而
translation_en:
…why, then, should there also be a shortage of them? Someone of old said, “An enlightened ruler values the five grains and holds gold and jade cheap.” It is also said, “The wealth produced by Heaven and Earth lies either with the government or with the people.” Thus the relative values of grain and gold rise and fall against one another; likewise, wealth held by the government and by the people tends to increase on one side as it diminishes on the other. Yet nowadays harvests vary between abundance and scarcity. Since grain is not always plentiful, one might expect gold sometimes to be in surplus, but shortages of it too are frequently reported. What, then, should be given priority to remedy this?

The realm now faces many troubles, and the treasuries are inadequately supplied. Those responsible for state finances have gone so far as to employ every expedient to remedy the situation, yet supplies remain insufficient. Meanwhile, the common people are in straitened circumstances, and we constantly hear it said, “The people’s resources are exhausted.” Can the saying that wealth lies either with the government or with the people be unworthy of belief?

Of late, His Majesty has been deeply concerned with agriculture and has given particular attention to state reserves. Each spring, when the weather grows mild, he issues an edict encouraging cultivation; whenever flood or drought strikes, he prays with utmost devotion. He scrutinizes provisions and supplies and exercises care in granting rewards. Even requirements for his own use are repeatedly reviewed and reduced. The annual savings amount to no less than several hundred thousand. The principle of increasing sources of revenue and restraining expenditure has thus been pursued to the utmost. Yet carrying out his benevolent intentions rests with the responsible officials. Might there be something in which their efforts fall short?

To establish one benefit is less effective than to eliminate one harm; to store wealth in the state is less effective than to store wealth among the people. Now we wish to eliminate whatever harms grain and gold, so that those above and those below may both benefit and…

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
俱足果何施而獲可耶爾諸生明於利
害之故贏縮之情其必有以畫此矣執
事者願聞其說
問功以才立名以功彰昔人所以建旂常
之勳而垂竹帛之譽良有由也然亦有
才猷未試功烈未究而褒然負天下之
望者何耶試畧評之偃息而樊魏談笑
而卻秦比量於千頃之陂寄跡於一絲
之釣者皆甘於儉德遠於榮名而當世
===
推之後世以為賢也豈亦有以自見者
耶奮興劉之志成輔晉之功其所樹立
固亦俊偉而始焉勤三顧於南陽來徵
書於東山抑何所自耶至於僅官省闥
而強宗寢其邪謀方下相麻而重臣損
其騶從戡亂正俗甚易易也果何道以
致之耶即如志先於憂樂誠信於華夷
者雖今之僕夫孺子莫不誦德美想風
采而在當時方為秀才為諫議政府未

者雖今之僕夫孺子莫不誦德美想風
采而在當時方爲秀才爲諫議政府未
punctuated:
俱足，果何施而獲可耶？爾諸生明於利害之故、贏縮之情，其必有以畫此矣。執事者願聞其說。

問：功以才立，名以功彰。昔人所以建旂常之勳，而垂竹帛之譽，良有由也。然亦有才猷未試、功烈未究，而褒然負天下之望者，何耶？試畧評之：偃息而樊魏，談笑而卻秦，比量於千頃之陂，寄跡於一絲之釣者，皆甘於儉德，遠於榮名，而當世推之，後世以為賢也，豈亦有以自見者耶？奮興劉之志，成輔晉之功，其所樹立固亦俊偉，而始焉勤三顧於南陽，來徵書於東山，抑何所自耶？至於僅官省闥，而強宗寢其邪謀；方下相麻，而重臣損其騶從，戡亂正俗甚易易也，果何道以致之耶？即如志先於憂樂、誠信於華夷者，雖今之僕夫孺子，莫不誦德美、想風采，而在當時，方為秀才、為諫議，政府未
translation_en:
…and both have enough, what measures would actually achieve a satisfactory result? You scholars understand the causes of benefit and harm and the circumstances of surplus and shortage; surely you can devise a plan for this. Those conducting the examination wish to hear your explanation.

Question: Accomplishments are established through ability, and reputation is made illustrious through accomplishments. There were sound reasons why men of old achieved merits worthy of inscription on banners and left reputations recorded on bamboo and silk. Yet there were also men whose abilities and plans had not been tested and whose achievements had not fully unfolded, but who already bore, with distinction, the hopes of all under Heaven. Why was this? Try briefly to assess them. There was one who, resting at ease, served as a protective barrier for Wei [?]; one who, amid conversation and laughter, repelled Qin; one who was likened to a reservoir of a thousand qing; and one who withdrew into a life of fishing with a single thread. All were content with modest virtue and kept far from glory and fame, yet their contemporaries esteemed them and later generations considered them worthy. Did they, too, have some means of making their qualities evident?

Those who roused themselves with the resolve to restore the Liu house, or accomplished the task of supporting Jin, certainly established outstanding achievements. But at the outset, what prompted the three visits to Nanyang and brought letters of summons to Dongshan? Then there were those who merely held office within the palace precincts, yet caused a powerful imperial kinsman to abandon his wicked schemes; or whose appointment as chief councilor had only just been proclaimed on hemp paper, yet caused a powerful minister to reduce his mounted attendants. Quelling disorder and correcting public conduct were exceedingly easy for them. By what means did they achieve this?

Consider also those whose resolve was to be first in anxiety and last in enjoyment, or whose sincerity won the trust of Chinese and non-Chinese alike. Even servants and children today all praise their virtue and imagine their bearing. Yet at the time, they were only a scholar or a Remonstrator, their entry into the chief council still…

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
登輿情咸屬此又何以也豈其素所操
持者固自有在而勳名之超卓不專待
於才耶彼望繫蒼生識者輕之功成大
將敵人易之則名與才似皆不足恃也
君子之欲懋宏業流芳譽者宜何所適
從耶將砥礪之節經綸之具預養而兼
全古之人必有可法者矣諸士博覽遺
編景行往哲所學之大宜無出於此者
請遂言之以觀尚友之志
===
問古今言學者必貴用世嘗覽載記蘇秦
起閭巷說六國指其國中阨塞虛實如
指掌賈誼自洛陽見漢文言諸侯强盛
當割後皆如誼言韓信自追所還勸高
祖入關取三秦弱項羽卒用信策夫蘇
君說客賈生少年韓淮陰武夫固儒者
弗道而其言皆售豈其於天下大勢有
所獨見歟乃諸士固為用世来也其大
勢將有可言者歟今在北邊東有薊鎮

編景行往哲所學之大宜無出於此者

===
問古今言學者必貴用世嘗覽載記蘇秦
起閭巷說六國指其國中阨塞虛實如
指掌賈誼自洛陽見漢文言諸侯强盛
當割後皆如誼言韓信自追所還勸高
祖入關取三秦弱項羽卒用信策夫蘇

所獨見歟乃諸士固為用世來也其大
勢將有可言者歟今在北邊東有薊鎮
punctuated:
登，輿情咸屬，此又何以也？豈其素所操持者固自有在，而勳名之超卓不專待於才耶？彼望繫蒼生，識者輕之；功成大將，敵人易之，則名與才似皆不足恃也。君子之欲懋宏業、流芳譽者，宜何所適從耶？將砥礪之節、經綸之具，預養而兼全，古之人必有可法者矣。諸士博覽遺編，景行往哲，所學之大，宜無出於此者。請遂言之，以觀尚友之志。

問：古今言學者，必貴用世。嘗覽載記，蘇秦起閭巷，說六國，指其國中阨塞虛實，如指掌。賈誼自洛陽見漢文，言諸侯强盛當割，後皆如誼言。韓信自追所還，勸高祖入關，取三秦，弱項羽，卒用信策。夫蘇君說客，賈生少年，韓淮陰武夫，固儒者弗道，而其言皆售，豈其於天下大勢有所獨見歟？乃諸士固為用世來也，其大勢將有可言者歟？今在北邊，東有薊鎮
translation_en:
…entered the highest councils, yet public expectations already rested unanimously upon them: why was this? Was it because the principles they had consistently upheld possessed a firm foundation of their own, so that their outstanding achievements and fame did not depend solely upon talent? There were those upon whom the hopes of the common people rested, yet discerning men thought little of them; others achieved distinction as great generals, yet their enemies held them in contempt. Thus reputation and talent alike seem insufficient to rely upon. What course, then, should a gentleman follow who wishes to accomplish great undertakings and leave an enduring good name? To cultivate beforehand and possess in full both disciplined integrity and the abilities needed to order the realm, there must surely be men of antiquity whom one can take as models. You gentlemen have read widely in the writings handed down and look up to the worthy thinkers of the past. Surely nothing in your learning is greater than this. Please explain fully, so that we may see your aspiration to befriend the worthies of antiquity.

Question: Those who discuss learning, past and present, invariably prize its application in public affairs. Reading historical accounts, I have observed that Su Qin rose from the common lanes and persuaded the six states; he could point out their strategic passes and their strengths and weaknesses as clearly as the palm of his hand. Jia Yi came from Luoyang to an audience with Emperor Wen of Han and said that the feudal princes were powerful and their territories should be reduced. Subsequent events all bore out his words. Han Xin, after returning from the place where he had been overtaken by his pursuer [?], urged Gaozu to enter the passes, seize the Three Qin territories, and weaken Xiang Yu. In the end, Gaozu adopted Xin’s strategy. Master Su was a traveling persuader, Master Jia a young man, and Han Xin of Huaiyin a military man—people whom Confucian scholars ordinarily would not discuss. Yet their proposals all won acceptance. Could it be that they possessed unique insight into the overall configuration of affairs in the realm? Now you gentlemen have indeed come with the intention of serving in public affairs. Might you have something to say about that overall configuration? At present, on the northern frontier, there is the Ji garrison command to the east…

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
西有宣大二鎮此三鎮最急昔宣大督
臣屢議設垣墻塹堡之險今可據以拒
虜歟又有欲大城
京後者亦可行歟經畧薊鎮者以為先拊循
三衛內服而後可外禦然歟又有謂薊
鎮邊獨長而古北諸口最要備寡則力
弱防弛則勢殆欲多設兵屯可歟曩倭
夷實首難浙直間邇歲幸漸休息而又
千里被水患民無寧居茲冦轉而之閩
===
廣急矣頃江右尤急有司日以警聞此
何以乂安之歟夫武備日弛而冦患充
斥非練兵不可濟茲可舉而行之否歟
上明聖詔旨嘗切責諸臣當事者宜訓練有序
矣而未臻厥效何歟或言南北勢殊所
為練者不同然歟或又言北當責將帥
而南當責守令果若是異歟又别有究
極根本之論歟在古聖世未嘗無蠻夷
冦賊之患貴制禦有道耳其陳之毋忽

京後者亦可行歟經畧薊鎮者以為先拊循

夷實首難浙直閩迺歲幸漸休息而又
千里被水患民無寍居茲寇轉而之閩
===
廣急矣頃江右尤急有司日以警聞此
何以人安之歟夫武備日弛而寇患亢
斥非練兵不可濟茲可舉而行之否歟
上明聖詔旨嘗切責諸臣當事者宜訓練有序
矣而未臻厥效何歟或言南北勢殊所
為練者不同然歟或又言北當責將帥
而南當責守令果若是異歟又別有究
極根本之論歟在古聖世未嘗無蠻夷
寇賊之患貴制禦有道耳其陳之毋忽
punctuated: 西有宣大二鎮，此三鎮最急。昔宣大督臣屢議設垣墻塹堡之險，今可據以拒虜歟？又有欲大城京後者，亦可行歟？經畧薊鎮者以為先拊循三衛內服，而後可外禦，然歟？又有謂薊鎮邊獨長，而古北諸口最要，備寡則力弱，防弛則勢殆，欲多設兵屯，可歟？曩倭夷實首難浙直間，邇歲幸漸休息，而又千里被水患，民無寧居。茲冦轉而之閩廣，急矣！頃江右尤急，有司日以警聞，此何以乂安之歟？夫武備日弛，而冦患充斥，非練兵不可濟，茲可舉而行之否歟？上明聖，詔旨嘗切責諸臣，當事者宜訓練有序矣，而未臻厥效，何歟？或言南北勢殊，所為練者不同，然歟？或又言北當責將帥，而南當責守令，果若是異歟？又别有究極根本之論歟？在古聖世，未嘗無蠻夷冦賊之患，貴制禦有道耳。其陳之，毋忽！
translation_en:
…to the west are the two defense commands of Xuanfu and Datong. These three commands face the most urgent threats. Formerly, the supreme commanders overseeing Xuanfu and Datong repeatedly proposed constructing defensive walls, moats, and forts. Can these now be relied upon to repel the northern invaders? Others wish to build extensive fortifications behind the capital. Is this also practicable? Those planning the defense of the Jizhou command believe that the Three Guards must first be soothed and brought into submission, and only then can external attacks be resisted. Is this so? Others say that the frontier of the Jizhou command is exceptionally long, and that the passes at Gubei and elsewhere are the most vital: scant defensive preparations mean inadequate strength, while lax defenses make the position precarious. They wish to establish more troop encampments. Would this be feasible?

Previously, the Japanese raiders first stirred up trouble in Zhejiang and the Metropolitan Region. In recent years, fortunately, there has gradually been some respite; yet floods have afflicted a thousand li of territory, leaving the people without peaceful dwellings. Now these raiders have turned toward Fujian and Guangdong, and the situation is urgent! Recently, Jiangxi has been in still greater danger, and the responsible officials report alarms daily. How can order and peace be restored there?

Military preparedness grows laxer by the day, while raiders overrun the land; without training troops, nothing can be accomplished. Can this now be undertaken and put into practice? His Majesty is enlightened and sagely, and his edicts have sternly reproached his ministers. Those responsible ought therefore to have brought training into proper order. Why has it still failed to produce results? Some say that conditions in the south and north differ, and that the training required is accordingly different. Is this so? Others say that in the north responsibility should be placed upon the generals, while in the south it should be placed upon the prefects and county magistrates. Is the distinction really as they say? Or is there some further argument that gets to the very root of the matter? Even in the age of the ancient sages, troubles from non-Chinese peoples, raiders, and bandits were never absent. What matters is simply having the proper means to control and resist them. Set forth your views, and do not treat this lightly!

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
事君能致其身
成鍾音
同考試官主事羅批人臣致身事君此作明
暢精切宜錄以式
同考試官都給事中張批此作說人臣致身之心
明盡可誦
同考試官都給事中丘批致身事君此人臣之心
===
也是作體認親切造語精當發盡誠意透徹非
懷忠藎者不能宜式多士
同考試官編修胡批發揮人臣事君之心精
切而詞復雅馴可式
同考試官編修王批此作發揮人臣致身之
義精確懇到蓋真能允蹈者

盡忠者取之

punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

事君能致其身

成鍾音

同考試官主事羅批：「人臣致身事君，此作明暢精切，宜錄以式。」

同考試官都給事中張批：「此作說人臣致身之心，明盡可誦。」

同考試官都給事中丘批：「致身事君，此人臣之心也。是作體認親切，造語精當，發盡誠意，透徹，非懷忠藎者不能，宜式多士。」

同考試官編修胡批：「發揮人臣事君之心，精切，而詞復雅馴，可式。」

同考試官編修王批：「此作發揮人臣致身之義，精確懇到，蓋真能允蹈者。」

考試官學士董批：「發致字義有獨見，必能盡忠者，取之。」

考試官大學士袁批：「誦其文，忠義之心勃然」
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“In serving his ruler, he can devote his whole person.”

Cheng Zhongyin 成鍾音

Comment by Associate Examiner Luo, Bureau Secretary: “On a minister’s devoting himself to the service of his ruler, this essay is clear, fluent, precise, and incisive. It should be recorded as a model.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Chief Supervising Secretary: “This essay explains clearly and fully the resolve with which a minister devotes himself. It is worthy of recitation.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Qiu, Chief Supervising Secretary: “To devote oneself to serving one’s ruler—this is the heart of a minister. This essay shows an intimate understanding and uses precise, apt language. It gives full and penetrating expression to sincerity. Only someone possessed of devoted loyalty could have written it. It should serve as a model for the many scholars.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Compiler: “Its exposition of a minister’s heart in serving his ruler is precise and incisive, and its language is also elegant and polished. It may serve as a model.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Compiler: “This essay develops the meaning of a minister’s devoting himself with precision, earnestness, and thoroughness. Its author surely is someone who can truly put this into practice.”

Comment by Examiner Dong, Academician: “He shows distinctive insight in expounding the meaning of the word ‘devote.’ He must be someone capable of the utmost loyalty. Accept him.”

Comment by Examiner Yuan, Grand Secretary: “On reciting his essay, a spirit of loyalty and righteousness wells up…”

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
賢者言人臣誠以事君而克盡匪躬之義焉夫
人臣而自有其身事君必不誠也能致其身則
能致其誠於君矣其斯以為人臣之心乎昔子
夏居聖門文學之科故示人以學問之要曰君
子之於學求以盡倫也君子之於倫求以盡誠
也人倫莫大於事君而可以弗誠乎今夫君臣
天下之大分也以臣事君天下之大義也分之
所在則君尊臣卑身不可不役於君也義之所
在則君逸臣勞力不可不出於身也為人臣者
===
誠能知受君之爵非為其寵榮已也以身許之
則以身委之矣食君之祿非為其利養已也身
既在君則身非在我矣是故有官守者則知無
不為為無不力顧天下之休戚而身所不暇顧
也有言責者則知無不言言無不盡計國家之
利弊而身所不及計也是非不愛其身也君為
重則身為輕彼固知所擇矣亦非自忘其身也
君為貴則身為賤蓋已審之熟矣是之謂不貳
心之臣士之惇倫而知學者也子夏明此以立

punctuated: 賢者言人臣誠以事君，而克盡匪躬之義焉。夫人臣而自有其身，事君必不誠也；能致其身，則能致其誠於君矣。其斯以為人臣之心乎？昔子夏居聖門文學之科，故示人以學問之要曰：君子之於學，求以盡倫也；君子之於倫，求以盡誠也。人倫莫大於事君，而可以弗誠乎？今夫君臣，天下之大分也；以臣事君，天下之大義也。分之所在，則君尊臣卑，身不可不役於君也；義之所在，則君逸臣勞，力不可不出於身也。為人臣者，誠能知受君之爵，非為其寵榮已也，以身許之，則以身委之矣；食君之祿，非為其利養已也，身既在君，則身非在我矣。是故有官守者，則知無不為，為無不力，顧天下之休戚，而身所不暇顧也；有言責者，則知無不言，言無不盡，計國家之利弊，而身所不及計也。是非不愛其身也，君為重，則身為輕，彼固知所擇矣；亦非自忘其身也，君為貴，則身為賤，蓋已審之熟矣。是之謂不貳心之臣，士之惇倫而知學者也。子夏明此以立
translation_en:
The worthy explains that a minister serves his ruler with sincerity and thereby fully fulfills the duty of disregarding his own person. If a minister regards his person as his own possession, his service to his ruler will surely lack sincerity. If he can devote his person entirely, he can offer his utmost sincerity to his ruler. Is this not the disposition proper to a minister?

Formerly, Zixia distinguished himself in textual learning among the disciples of the Sage. Thus, in showing others the essentials of learning, he said: In learning, the gentleman seeks to fulfill his human relationships; in those relationships, he seeks to exercise the utmost sincerity. Among human relationships, none is greater than service to one’s ruler. How could one be insincere in it? The relationship between ruler and minister is the great distinction of rank under Heaven; serving one’s ruler as a minister is the great duty under Heaven. By that distinction, the ruler is exalted and the minister lowly, so the minister must place his person at the ruler’s service. By that duty, the ruler rests while the minister labors, so the minister must exert his own strength.

If a minister truly understands that receiving rank from his ruler is not intended to confer favor and glory upon himself, then, having pledged his person to the ruler, he entrusts it to him entirely. Drawing the ruler’s stipend is not intended for his own material support: since his person belongs to his ruler, it no longer belongs to himself. Thus, those charged with official duties undertake everything they know ought to be done and exert themselves fully in everything they undertake. They attend to the well-being and suffering of all under Heaven, with no leisure to attend to themselves. Those charged with speaking out say everything they know and leave nothing unsaid. They consider what benefits or harms the state, without having occasion to consider themselves.

This does not mean that they do not cherish their own persons. When the ruler carries greater weight, their own persons carry less: they certainly know which to choose. Nor does it mean that they simply forget themselves. When the ruler is held precious, their own persons count as little: they have already considered this thoroughly. Such men are called ministers of undivided loyalty, scholars who faithfully uphold human relationships and understand learning. Zixia made this clear in order to establish…

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
□□哉記有之曰子夏聖門之高弟也入見夫
子之道而說蓋其篤信聖人曾子而下鮮或之
及故其所述稱者皆確守師說而致身一語固
聖人事君以忠乎出也夫盡心之謂忠盡誠之
謂致身身心合一人臣之大訓也人能口誦心
惟而允蹈之尚何臣節之不貞臣道之不淑哉
吁以此為防而後世猶有私便其身圖者
悠久無疆
華啓直
===
同考試官署郎中吳批莊重典雅精於中庸義
者錄之
同考試官檢討吳批體格渾融語意精密文
之極作也
同考試官編修張批以雄健之詞而發真切
之見非老學不能到
同考試官修撰丁批詞氣古雅思致不凡宜
錄以式多士
考試官學士董批說聖人與天地同體處得旨

□□哉！記有之曰：「子夏，聖門之高弟也，入見夫子之道而說。」蓋其篤信聖人，曾子而下鮮或之及。故其所述稱者，皆確守師說，而致身一語，固聖人事君以忠乎出也。夫盡心之謂忠，盡誠之謂致身，身心合一，人臣之大訓也。人能口誦心惟而允蹈之，尚何臣節之不貞、臣道之不淑哉？吁！以此為防，而後世猶有私便其身圖者。

悠久無疆
華啓直

translation_en:
…[two illegible characters]! A record states: “Zixia was an outstanding disciple of the sage’s school. He entered, beheld the Master’s Way, and delighted in it.” Such was his steadfast faith in the sage that few, from Zengzi onward, could match him. Thus everything he expounded and commended firmly upheld his teacher’s teachings; the expression “devote one’s person” surely derives from the sage’s teaching that one should serve one’s ruler with loyalty [?]. To give one’s whole heart is called loyalty; to give one’s utmost sincerity is called devoting one’s person. Uniting body and mind is the great instruction for a ruler’s servants. If a person can recite this aloud, ponder it in his heart, and faithfully put it into practice, how could his integrity as a minister be anything but steadfast, or his conduct as a minister anything but good? Alas! Even with this as a safeguard, later generations still produced those who schemed for their own personal convenience [?].

“Enduring Long, Without Bounds”
By Hua Qizhi.

Associate Examiner Wu, Acting Bureau Director, comments: “Dignified and classically elegant. It shows mastery of the meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean. Select it.”

Associate Examiner Wu, Hanlin Examining Editor, comments: “Its form is thoroughly integrated, and its language and meaning are refined and precise. This is a supreme achievement in composition.”

Associate Examiner Zhang, Hanlin Compiler, comments: “It expresses genuine and penetrating insights in powerful, vigorous language. Only a seasoned scholar could attain this.”

Associate Examiner Ding, Hanlin Senior Compiler, comments: “Its diction and spirit possess classical elegance, and its conception is exceptional. It should be selected as a model for the many scholars.”

Examiner Dong, Hanlin Academician, comments: “Its explanation of how the sage forms one body with Heaven and Earth grasps the essential meaning.”

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
考試官大學士袁批善發天地聖人之蘊
至誠功業之極與天地相為無窮焉夫天地之
道貞觀者也至誠而極于悠久矣其不與天地
為無窮哉中庸此章言天道也若曰論道者必
本于天地論功業者必歸于聖人今聖人之至
誠也自其積之而為博厚固足以配地矣然非
一時之積而已也自其發之而為高明固足以
配天矣然非一時之發而已也積之不已而大
順所敷有以成優柔平中之化發之不已而至
===
治所及有以垂長永貞固之休自其博厚之體
而至靜有常地之無疆本如是者聖人之博厚
則引之不見其始要之不見其終實與坤元而
無間焉自其高明之體而運行不息天之無疆
本如是者聖人之高明則推之莫測其端究之
莫測其至實與乾元而無貳焉是蓋萬古常存
者天地也萬世永賴者聖人也三才于是而並
立宰持萬古者天地也撫御萬世者聖人也三
極于是而同歸此天地自然之體非聖人有所

At their utmost, the achievements of perfect sincerity endure without limit together with Heaven and Earth. The Way of Heaven and Earth manifests itself in constancy; through perfect sincerity it attains the utmost in enduring continuance. Would it not endure without limit together with Heaven and Earth? This chapter of the Doctrine of the Mean speaks of the Way of Heaven. It is as though it said: those who discuss the Way must take Heaven and Earth as their foundation; those who discuss achievements must ultimately turn to the sage. Now, the sage’s perfect sincerity, accumulating into breadth and depth, is assuredly sufficient to match Earth. Yet this is no mere momentary accumulation. Manifesting itself in loftiness and brilliance, it is assuredly sufficient to match Heaven. Yet this is no mere momentary manifestation. Through unceasing accumulation, wherever supreme accord spreads, it brings about a transformation that is gentle, harmonious, and balanced. Through unceasing manifestation, wherever consummate government reaches, it bequeaths blessings that are lasting, constant, and firm. In its broad and deep substance, Earth is utterly still and constant: such is the inherent character of its boundlessness. As for the sage’s breadth and depth, trace it backward and its beginning cannot be seen; seek its conclusion and its end cannot be seen. It is truly inseparable from the primal power of kun, Earth. In its lofty and brilliant substance, Heaven moves unceasingly: such is the inherent character of its boundlessness. As for the sage’s loftiness and brilliance, trace it back and its origin cannot be fathomed; investigate it fully and its furthest reach cannot be fathomed. It is truly one with the primal power of qian, Heaven. Thus, what abides through all antiquity is Heaven and Earth; what ten thousand generations forever depend upon is the sage. The Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—thereby stand together. What governs and sustains all ages is Heaven and Earth; what nurtures and rules ten thousand generations is the sage. The three ultimate principles thereby converge. This is the natural constitution of Heaven and Earth, not something that the sage …

…force himself into accord with them. Can the ultimate achievement of perfect sincerity indeed reach such heights! In general, Heaven and Earth bring forth sages to assist their transforming activity, and sages stand alongside Heaven and Earth to fulfill their capacities. From emperors and kings downward, all receive their charge from Heaven and Earth. By comprehensively ordering their Way and assisting what is fitting to them, sages provide immense support to Heaven and Earth. text:

夫臺也者察符瑞而候祲祥者也文王嘗以民
力爲臺焉沼也者時觀游而節勞逸者也文王
亦嘗以民力爲沼焉夫役民之力能使民忘其
勞亦難矣安能得其歡乎文王之民吾見載色
載笑翕然其交歡也能使民從其令亦足矣安
能致其樂乎文王之民吾見以夷以懌油然其

translation_en:
…even a sage cannot always fulfill his heart’s desire. Why not consider King Wen? A terrace is a place for observing auspicious tokens and watching for baleful and favorable portents; King Wen once employed the people’s labor to build a terrace. A pond is a place for viewing and recreation at appropriate times, regulating the balance between exertion and repose; King Wen also once employed the people’s labor to make a pond. When employing the people’s strength, even making them forget their toil is difficult. How could one win their delight? Yet among King Wen’s people I see beaming faces and laughter, all united in mutual delight. Merely getting the people to obey one’s commands would be enough. How could one bring them joy? Yet among King Wen’s people I see ease and contentment, their shared joy arising spontaneously. United in heart and delighting in one another, they naturally unite their strength to help one another; sharing feelings and rejoicing together, they naturally join their voices in mutual encouragement. It was fitting that the terrace and pond should be completed in scarcely any time.

The people said: “Our king’s virtue has long reached the spirits. This lofty terrace rose swiftly without haste: surely its accomplishment was the work of divine planning, not an achievement in which the common people could claim a share. By naming it the Numinous Terrace, can we not make manifest the marvel of unseen assistance?” They also said: “Our king’s beneficence has reached spirits and men, bringing harmony. This deep pond was completed without urgency: surely this was the responsive working of divine transformation, not something human strength could bring about. By naming it the Numinous Pond, can we not display the achievement of hidden aid?”

From this we know that King Wen did not go against the people to gratify his desires, and so he necessarily won their hearts; he did not depart from the Way to seek praise, and so he necessarily won their acclaim. Is not the principle that the worthy enjoy themselves only afterward borne out by this sage? I have read in the transmitted commentary: “King Wen possessed abundant virtue and extended his beneficence widely; he established goodness [?] and dispensed kindness. In his time, the myriad things did not lose their proper natures, and all under Heaven missed no season for bringing to completion…”

text:

王道以天下各得其養為極至也上爻之元吉
以之宜聖人深致其贊歟象傳之意若曰人君
之養天下也固貴乎盡其道而尤貴乎得其時
道有未善則治有所阻不可以言成也時有未
值則化有所限不可以言大成也今謂之元吉
是其于道也既以得井養之義矣元吉而在上
是其于時也又復當井養之終矣吾見出于朝
廷者德意充周既無不被之澤施于海宇者仁
===

如育于天之覆如育于地之載皞皞乎各遂其

以是而考其成焉可也雖然周公于上爻之元

punctuated: 聖人舉井上爻之占，而贊其為王道之極焉。夫王道以天下各得其養為極至也。上爻之元吉，以之，宜聖人深致其贊歟！象傳之意若曰：人君之養天下也，固貴乎盡其道，而尤貴乎得其時。道有未善，則治有所阻，不可以言成也；時有未值，則化有所限，不可以言大成也。今謂之元吉，是其于道也，既以得井養之義矣；元吉而在上，是其于時也，又復當井養之終矣。吾見出于朝廷者，德意充周，既無不被之澤；施于海宇者，仁恩浹洽，自無不獲之民。由庶而富也，由富而教也，法制品節之詳，已至而極其至；由動而變也，由變而化也，鼓舞作興之術，已深而極其深。是蓋上之養民，如天之無不覆，如地之無不載，蕩蕩乎各適其願，曾靡有于或遺；民之見養于上，如育于天之覆，如育于地之載，皞皞乎各遂其生，又何有于不足？信乎盡善盡美，而不可以復加矣！非養道之大成而何？然則取法于井者，亦以是而考其成焉可也。雖然，周公于上爻之元
translation_en:
The sage cites the prognostication for the top line of the Well hexagram and praises it as the culmination of the Kingly Way. The Kingly Way reaches its highest fulfillment when everyone under Heaven receives nourishment. The top line’s supreme good fortune rests on this [?]; fittingly, the sage praises it so profoundly! The Commentary on the Images seems to say: In nourishing all under Heaven, a ruler must certainly value fully realizing the Way, but must especially value meeting the proper time. If the Way is not yet perfected, government encounters obstacles and cannot be called accomplished. If the time has not yet arrived, transformation remains limited and cannot be called a great accomplishment. Now, to speak of “supreme good fortune” means that, with respect to the Way, the principle of nourishment represented by the Well has already been realized. That supreme good fortune occurs at the top means that, with respect to timing, nourishment represented by the Well has also reached its culminating stage.

I see virtuous intentions issuing from the court, abundant and all-embracing, with no one beyond the reach of their beneficence; humane kindness extends throughout the realm, permeating it so thoroughly that none of the people fails to receive it. From making the people numerous to making them prosperous, and from making them prosperous to educating them, the detailed ordering of laws, institutions, distinctions, and regulations has reached the utmost refinement. From stirring them to bringing about change, and from change to transformation, the methods of inspiring and invigorating them have reached the utmost depth. Thus, the ruler’s nourishment of the people resembles Heaven, which leaves nothing uncovered, and Earth, which leaves nothing unsupported. In this vast abundance, each finds satisfaction for his wishes, and none is left out. Nourished by their ruler, the people are as though nurtured beneath Heaven’s covering and upon Earth’s support. In joyous contentment, each fulfills his life: what insufficiency could remain? Truly, this is perfect goodness and perfect beauty, to which nothing further can be added! What could it be but the great accomplishment of the Way of nourishment? Those who take the Well as their model may therefore use this to assess their accomplishment. title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
設位而易行乎其中矣成其能者不有待于聖
人乎大傳之意若曰聖人之于造化也固不假
易以知其理尤必作易以賛其功是故積陽之
氣而確然示人者天也天則位乎上焉積陰之
質而隤然示人者地也地則位乎下焉對待之
體立而一闔一闢自有以寓推行之漸盈虛消
息已于此乎開其先矣高卑之極陳而一升一
降自有以運訢合之機絪縕摩盪實于此乎啓
其兆矣夫天地設位固易理之原也然垂法象
===
之顯者雖在于天地而洩造化之秘者實資于
聖人于是聖人本乾坤自然之理而模寫于書
以致彌綸之道察變化形見之端而發揮于易
以成參賛之功立象以盡意聖人之精也而實
所以闡天地之精以體其撰焉以效其動焉開
物成務而天地之心盡矣繫辭以盡言聖人之
蘊也而實所以究天地之蘊以極其深焉以研
其幾焉通志成業而天地之事畢矣非聖人成
天地之能而何哉雖然聖人非有所加于天地

聖人于是聖人本乾坤自然之理而模寫于書
以致彌綸之道察變化形見之端而發揮于易
以成參贊之功立象以盡意聖人之精也而實

物成務而天地之心盡矣繫辭以盡言聖人之
蘊也而實所以究天地之蘊以極其深焉以研
其幾焉通志成業而天地之事畢矣非聖人成
天地之能而何哉雖然聖人非有所加于天地
punctuated: 設位，而易行乎其中矣。成其能者，不有待于聖人乎？大傳之意若曰：聖人之于造化也，固不假易以知其理，尤必作易以賛其功。是故積陽之氣而確然示人者，天也；天則位乎上焉。積陰之質而隤然示人者，地也；地則位乎下焉。對待之體立，而一闔一闢，自有以寓推行之漸，盈虛消息已于此乎開其先矣。高卑之極陳，而一升一降，自有以運訢合之機，絪縕摩盪實于此乎啓其兆矣。夫天地設位，固易理之原也。然垂法象之顯者，雖在于天地，而洩造化之秘者，實資于聖人。于是聖人本乾坤自然之理，而模寫于書，以致彌綸之道；察變化形見之端，而發揮于易，以成參賛之功。立象以盡意，聖人之精也，而實所以闡天地之精，以體其撰焉，以效其動焉，開物成務，而天地之心盡矣。繫辭以盡言，聖人之蘊也，而實所以究天地之蘊，以極其深焉，以研其幾焉，通志成業，而天地之事畢矣。非聖人成天地之能而何哉？雖然，聖人非有所加于天地
translation_en:
…take their appointed positions, and change operates within them. Does the fulfillment of their capacities not await the sage? The meaning of the Great Commentary is as if to say: in relation to creation and transformation, the sage certainly does not need the Changes to understand their principles; yet he must compose the Changes to assist their work. Thus, that which gathers the vital force of yang and manifests itself to people as firmness is Heaven; Heaven takes its position above. That which gathers the substance of yin and manifests itself to people as yieldingness is Earth; Earth takes its position below. Once their mutually opposed forms are established, each closing and opening inherently embodies a gradual process of onward movement: fullness and emptiness, waning and waxing, already have their beginnings here. Once the extremes of high and low are arrayed, each ascent and descent inherently sets in motion the mechanism of harmonious union: intermingling, mutual friction, and agitation indeed first show their signs here.

The establishment of Heaven and Earth in their positions is indeed the source of the principles of the Changes. Yet although Heaven and Earth display manifest patterns and images, the disclosure of the secrets of creation and transformation truly depends upon the sage. Accordingly, the sage takes the spontaneous principles of Qian and Kun as his basis and depicts them in a book, thereby fully realizing the Way that encompasses and orders all things. He observes the first visible signs of change and transformation and expounds them in the Changes, thereby accomplishing the work of participating in and assisting them.

To establish images so as to express meaning fully is the sage’s refined insight; in truth, it is the means by which he elucidates the refined essence of Heaven and Earth. By embodying their workings and representing their movements, he discloses the nature of things and brings affairs to completion, fully expressing the heart of Heaven and Earth. To append statements so as to give full expression in words is the sage’s profound understanding; in truth, it is the means by which he probes the hidden profundities of Heaven and Earth. By plumbing their depths and investigating their incipient movements, he makes intentions intelligible and brings undertakings to completion, fully accomplishing the affairs of Heaven and Earth. What could this be but the sage’s fulfillment of the capacities of Heaven and Earth? Even so, the sage does not add anything to Heaven and Earth…

也使德未光大吾見有所及亦有所不及矣堯

幅幀亦既長也而不冒之餘無一夫而不蒙其

考試官大學士袁批：堯德無能名，此足以名矣。

史臣賛帝德之廣運，以見其功之極也。甚矣，聖人德盛而化神也！則其四表之被、上下之格，固宜矣。此史臣賛放勳之大也。今夫言帝王之治者，至堯而極；言帝王之德者，亦至堯而極。何則？人君宅中而制外，則四表之遼邈，皆其所統御也。使德未光大，吾見有所及，亦有所不及矣。堯則有以顯被之焉。惟其積之也，淵乎其不匱，故其發之也，煥乎其有章。自西自東，疆域若是廣也，而照臨之下，無一處而不仰其明；自南自北，幅幀亦既長也，而不冒之餘，無一夫而不蒙其澤。是蓋遠而有外者，四表之地；大而無外者，聖人之德。堯其通天下為一身乎？人君體元而成位，則上下之寥廓，皆其所範圍也。使德未充周，吾見有所至，亦有所不至矣。堯則有以昭格之焉。惟其性之立也，渾乎其悉備，故其功之著也，巍乎其有成。天之所覆，莫能窮其際也，而所以□之者，通於高明而不禦；地之所載，莫能測

Examiner Yuan, Grand Secretary, comments: “None could find words to describe Yao’s virtue; this suffices to describe it.”

The court historian praises the vast reach of the emperor’s virtue to reveal the utmost extent of his achievement. How abundant is the sage’s virtue, and how wondrous his transforming influence! It is therefore only fitting that it should extend to the four outermost regions and reach above and below. This is the court historian’s praise of the greatness of Yao’s “far-reaching achievement.” Now, those who speak of the governance of emperors and kings find its culmination in Yao; those who speak of their virtue likewise find its culmination in Yao. Why is this? The ruler occupies the center and governs what lies beyond; thus even the distant reaches of the four outermost regions fall under his command. Were his virtue not radiant and great, I should find places it reached and places it did not. Yao, however, possessed the means to spread his virtue manifestly over them all. Only because its accumulation was deep and inexhaustible did its expression shine forth with such brilliance. From west to east, the territory was so broad, yet beneath his illumination there was not one place that did not look up to his radiance. From south to north, its extent [?] was also great, yet through its encompassing influence [?] there was not one man who did not receive his beneficence. Thus, the lands of the four outermost regions, though distant, have something beyond them; the sage’s virtue is so great that nothing lies beyond it. Did Yao not unite all under Heaven into a single body?

The ruler embodies the primal principle and takes his rightful position; thus the vast expanses above and below all fall within his compass. Were his virtue not full and all-pervading, I should find places it reached and places it did not. Yao, however, possessed the means to reach them all radiantly. Only because his established nature was wholly complete did his achievements stand forth so loftily accomplished. None can exhaust the bounds of what Heaven covers, yet that by which he □ it [?] penetrates Heaven’s loftiness and brightness without obstruction. As for what Earth bears, none can measure …

The gentleman sets forth the workings of the five forms of qi and thereby reveals their harmonious course. These five forms of qi belong to Heaven, and what governs their workings is timeliness. When they are complete and, moreover, properly ordered, is this not what constitutes their harmony? This is what Jizi meant when he set forth the categories to instruct King Wu. It is as though he were saying: To understand the evidence furnished by the various signs, one must investigate the relationship between Heaven and humanity. Thus yin and yang each serve as the root of the other, and from them the Five Phases arise. The Five Phases operate in succession, and through them the five forms of qi are diffused. Moisture produces rain; clearing produces sunshine: from these the myriad things obtain their moistening and warming. Expansion produces warmth; congealing produces cold; exhalation produces wind: from these the myriad things obtain their growth, storage, and movement. Yet amid their intermingling and mutual agitation, the workings of qi have fixed periods; amid contraction and expansion, coming and going, the creative transformations have their natural seasons. Is this not what is called timeliness? These indeed belong to Heaven. translation_en:
…[illegible character] arrive together [?], thus bringing their entirety into unity. Considered separately, none precedes and none follows; abundant in supreme harmony, each accords with its proper rule. Their endless cycle proceeds by gradual stages; their seamless, wondrous union allows them to operate together without conflict. What silently operates in Heaven finds a corresponding response among human beings, and therein lies the mechanism of influence and response. Can the ruler of all under Heaven fail to examine and verify this?
Yet although the way to examine and verify this lies in reasoning from Heaven and seeking confirmation among human beings, one who serves Heaven well does not cling to this alone. For what the sage exerts himself fully to accomplish lies in the human realm; what he dares not presume to determine lies with Heaven. Once he has exerted himself fully, if Heaven responds favorably, this is indeed the normal operation of principle, yet the sage dares not rely upon it. If Heaven has not responded favorably, this is indeed a variation in destiny, yet the sage dares not disregard it. Thus his virtue moves Heaven ever more deeply, and Heaven responds to him ever more fully. Herein lies the means by which the emperors and kings of antiquity reached Heaven. Only after attaining this may one discuss the meaning of the Great Plan.

鼎新之業所當興也。夫天子之宫，其室非一，則合百堵而築焉，以辨内外，極其規模之大也；天子之室，其戶非一，則分西南而列焉，以利出入，盡其法制之詳也。是室作而嗣祖之孝隆矣，樂成不因之哉？吾王高拱穆清，居處貴得其所也。今則蒞明堂而出治，顒昂之象肅焉；就路寢以即安，宥密之神頤焉。蓋昔妣祖之上下於庭、陟降於家者，皆於是而繩其武矣。吾王和德於上，笑語必有所適也。今則而康而色，弛以濟乎其張焉；如絲如綸，言以宣乎其心焉。蓋昔妣祖之泮奐爾游、優游爾休者，皆於是而衍其慶矣。夫一作室也，以繼先而孝道昭，以樂成而王制備，中興之烈不其偉哉？

抑宣王之所以善是室者有道焉：《雲漢》敬天，《庭燎》勤民，其本也；《鴻鴈》安宅，其基也；《車攻》講武，其垣墉甓茨也；而方叔、召虎、吉甫、申伯諸臣，又其楨榦也。則夫内修外攘，以復文武成康之業，宜矣。噫！此《斯干》之室所以與宅鎬營洛者媲美歟？
translation_en:
…the undertaking of renewal ought therefore to be set in motion. The Son of Heaven’s palace contains more than one chamber, so its many walls are built together to distinguish inner from outer, realizing the full grandeur of its plan. The Son of Heaven’s residence has more than one doorway, so doors are arranged on the west and south to facilitate entry and exit, fulfilling every detail of its prescribed design. With this residence built, the filial devotion with which he succeeds his ancestors is exalted. Would joy in its completion not follow? Our king sits with hands folded in solemn serenity; what matters in his dwelling is that he occupy his proper place. Now, when he comes to the Hall of Light to administer government, his lofty bearing inspires reverence; when he retires to the principal sleeping hall to rest, his profound and tranquil spirit is nourished. Wherever his ancestral mothers and forefathers once moved through the courtyard and went up and down within the household, he now follows in their footsteps. Our king manifests harmonious virtue on high, and his laughter and speech must find their fitting expression. Now, at ease and with a relaxed countenance, he tempers tension with repose; his words, like silken thread and cord, give expression to his heart. Wherever his ancestral mothers and forefathers once roamed freely and rested at leisure, he now perpetuates their blessings. In this single act of building a residence, filial devotion shines forth through continuing his predecessors’ work, and kingly institutions are made complete through rejoicing in its accomplishment. Is this achievement of dynastic restoration not magnificent?

Yet King Xuan had a way of bringing this residence to perfection. Reverence for Heaven, as in “The Milky Way” (Yunhan), and diligent care for the people, as in “Courtyard Torches” (Tingliao), were its root. Providing secure dwellings, as in “Wild Geese” (Hongyan), was its foundation. Practicing military arts, as in “Chariot Attack” (Chegong), supplied its enclosing walls, bricks, and thatch. And the ministers Fang Shu, Shao Hu, Jifu, and Shen Bo were its supporting posts and beams. It was fitting, then, that by cultivating order within and repelling threats from without, he restored the achievements of Kings Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang. Ah! Is this why the residence celebrated in “The Stream” (Si gan) could rival in beauty the establishment of the capital at Hao and the building of Luo?

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
德不尤著乎吾見和順發其華而臨下有赫蓋
天地將為昭焉是于丕顯而作求之有以覲允
文之耿光也篤實呈其輝而旁燭無疆蓋日月
合其明焉是于丕承而緝煕之有以揚無競之
大烈也吾王心德如此有不恊于上下哉是故
觀諸在野而民異其情難乎其宜之也然明德
所感莫不尊親令之而即行也動之而即化也
萬民和於野雝雝乎從欲之治矣觀諸在朝而
人異其位亦難乎其宜之也然明德所孚罔不
===
祗若志焉以之同也道焉以之合也百官和於
朝藹藹乎媚茲之忱矣夫天之所命徵諸民人
而已天之所與徵諸福祿而已由是而純嘏錫
焉繁祉介焉尊為天子而祿以天下者將多益
之矣非王之所昭受者乎戬穀綏焉釐宜集焉
富有四海而祿食萬方者將永享之矣非王之
所靈承者乎吁此可以見天人相與之際矣抑
此詩也說者以為答鳧鷖而作也今觀鳧鷖之
篇四言福祿是君述已之福乎臣也而此詩曰

篇四言福禄是君述已之福乎臣也而此詩曰
punctuated: 德不尤著乎？吾見和順發其華，而臨下有赫，蓋天地將為昭焉。是于丕顯而作求之，有以覲允文之耿光也。篤實呈其輝，而旁燭無疆，蓋日月合其明焉。是于丕承而緝煕之，有以揚無競之大烈也。吾王心德如此，有不恊于上下哉？是故觀諸在野，而民異其情，難乎其宜之也；然明德所感，莫不尊親，令之而即行也，動之而即化也。萬民和於野，雝雝乎從欲之治矣！觀諸在朝，而人異其位，亦難乎其宜之也；然明德所孚，罔不祗若，志焉以之同也，道焉以之合也。百官和於朝，藹藹乎媚茲之忱矣！夫天之所命，徵諸民人而已；天之所與，徵諸福祿而已。由是而純嘏錫焉，繁祉介焉，尊為天子而祿以天下者，將多益之矣，非王之所昭受者乎？戬穀綏焉，釐宜集焉，富有四海而祿食萬方者，將永享之矣，非王之所靈承者乎？吁！此可以見天人相與之際矣。抑此詩也，說者以為答《鳧鷖》而作也。今觀《鳧鷖》之篇，四言福祿，是君述已之福乎臣也，而此詩曰
translation_en:
…is his virtue not especially manifest? I see harmony and accord bringing forth their flowering, shining splendidly upon those below; Heaven and Earth themselves will make this radiance manifest. Thus, seeking to carry forward what is greatly illustrious, he displays the brilliant light of his truly cultivated virtue. His earnestness and integrity reveal their radiance, illuminating all around without limit; sun and moon join their brightness with his. Thus, carrying forward his great inheritance and continually making it shine, he proclaims his unrivalled achievements. With our king’s inward virtue like this, could there be any lack of concord with those above and below?

Consider, then, those in the countryside: the people differ in their dispositions, and it is difficult to deal fittingly with them all. Yet, moved by his luminous virtue, all revere and cherish him. When he commands them, they immediately act; when he stirs them, they are immediately transformed. The myriad people are harmonious in the countryside: how concordant is this government that accords with their desires! Consider those at court: men differ in their positions, and it is likewise difficult to deal fittingly with them all. Yet, won over by his luminous virtue, all respectfully comply. Through it their purposes become one, and through it their ways accord. The hundred officials are harmonious at court: how abundant is their sincere devotion to him!

Heaven’s bestowal of its mandate is verified simply by the people; Heaven’s favour is verified simply by blessings and emoluments. Hence great blessings are bestowed and abundant good fortune attends him. Exalted as Son of Heaven, with all under Heaven as his emolument, he will receive still greater bounty. Is this not what the king receives in splendour? Prosperity and goodness bring him peace, and blessings fittingly gather upon him. Possessing the wealth of the Four Seas and drawing sustenance from the myriad regions, he will enjoy these forever. Is this not what the king receives through divine favour? Ah! Here we can discern the point at which Heaven and humankind respond to one another.

Now, interpreters hold that this ode was composed in response to Wild Ducks and Gulls (Fu yi). Looking at Wild Ducks and Gulls, we find that it speaks four times of blessings and emoluments: this is the ruler recounting his own blessings to his ministers. But this ode says…

…“[?] emoluments,” “a hundred blessings,” and “without limit”: these are the minister’s prayers for Heaven’s blessings upon his ruler. In that flourishing age, ruler and ministers trusted one another through virtue and were united in heart. Expressed in their poetry and songs, this vividly recalled the spirit of joyful, vigorous service under Tang Yao and Yu Shun. The age of Kings Cheng and Kang was acclaimed as the height of good government; its foundations were firm and its sources deep. The enduring mandate of the Ji royal house truly depended upon this. If later rulers achieved admirable government approaching that of Cheng and Kang, how would they measure up to what this poem celebrates?

不書之以示謹哉吾聞爵次定於王制儀命嚴
於周官其不可紊也久矣宋何爲者而以意爲
升降耶曹之會也謀伐鄭也戎行欲即蔡固先
於衛矣鄭之伐也行曹之謀也壇坫未寒衛復
先於蔡焉語其爵均之姬姓之侯也蔡之所以
先衛者以叔度之封自武王始而胡可列於衛
之下也遡其世均之文王之昭也衛之所以後
蔡者以康叔之封自成王始而豈宜加於蔡之
上也宋莊爲此無乃喜衛先至而進之以爲趨
===
事之勸怒蔡後至而抑之以爲不恪之懲乎殊

punctuated:
不書之以示謹哉？吾聞爵次定於王制，儀命嚴於周官，其不可紊也久矣。宋何爲者，而以意爲升降耶？曹之會也，謀伐鄭也，戎行欲即，蔡固先於衛矣。鄭之伐也，行曹之謀也，壇坫未寒，衛復先於蔡焉。語其爵，均之姬姓之侯也。蔡之所以先衛者，以叔度之封自武王始，而胡可列於衛之下也？遡其世，均之文王之昭也。衛之所以後蔡者，以康叔之封自成王始，而豈宜加於蔡之上也？宋莊爲此，無乃喜衛先至而進之，以爲趨事之勸，怒蔡後至而抑之，以爲不恪之懲乎？殊不知禮有設儀辨位，所以謹侯度也。以主會而進退列國，則大司馬所以等邦國者弗顧矣。觀聽之駭，其何以示衆庶哉？禮有防微杜漸，所以窒亂源也。以私意而誘沮諸姬，則大宗伯所以正邦國者弗恤矣。僭踰之啓，其何以令諸侯哉？故春秋紀會曹、伐鄭，如其所爲而不革者，彰蔡衛之失序以罪宋莊也，而聖人謹禮之意見矣。

抑宋之伐鄭，爲納突也。彼果於爲不義者，於紊
translation_en:
…fail to record it to demonstrate vigilance over ritual propriety? I have heard that precedence among noble ranks is fixed by royal institutions, and that ceremonial prescriptions are strictly set out in the Offices of Zhou. That these must not be thrown into disorder has long been established. What authority did Song possess to raise or lower others according to its own wishes? The meeting at Cao was held to plan an attack on Zheng. As military action approached, Cai certainly preceded Wei. The attack on Zheng carried out the plan made at Cao; yet before the ceremonial platforms and stands had even grown cold, Wei once again preceded Cai. In rank, both were marquises of the Ji surname. Cai preceded Wei because Shudu’s enfeoffment dated from King Wu: how could Cai be placed below Wei? In lineage, both belonged to the zhao generation descended from King Wen. Wei followed Cai because Kangshu’s enfeoffment dated from King Cheng: how could Wei properly be placed above Cai? In doing this, was Duke Zhuang of Song perhaps pleased that Wei arrived first and promoted it to encourage prompt attendance to affairs, while angered that Cai arrived later and demoted it to punish disrespect?

He utterly failed to understand that ritual establishes ceremonies and distinguishes positions in order to safeguard the standards governing the feudal lords. By using his position as host of the meeting to advance or demote the states, he disregarded the means by which the Grand Marshal ranked the states. Such conduct shocked all who saw or heard of it: what example could it offer the people? Ritual guards against the slightest beginnings of wrongdoing and arrests its gradual growth in order to block disorder at its source. By using his private preferences to encourage or discourage the Ji rulers, he disregarded the means by which the Minister of Rites set the states in proper order. By opening the way to usurpation and overstepping of rank, how could he command the feudal lords? Thus, in recording the meeting at Cao and the attack on Zheng, the Spring and Autumn Annals retained the order in which events occurred without altering it, exposing the disruption of precedence between Cai and Wei in order to condemn Duke Zhuang of Song. Here the Sage’s intention to safeguard ritual propriety becomes manifest.
