額之外以求足乎金而卒未嘗足何也
punctuated: 人治天下，能使菽粟如水火，而猶重之也。此晁錯謂明君貴五穀而賤金玉，其說信矣。顧今之時，則有不然者。三尺童子，授金而投之，忻然咲而不忍釋。天下之愛金，類若此。至於五穀，乃或視輕焉。死生飽餒之繫，不遑恤，而顧汲汲焉重金者，何也？夫固有所用之也。自金之用日益侈，而上下之交征也日益甚，粟日以賤，而金日以詘，其勢必至於俱困而後已。司馬光曰：「天地生財，止有此數，不在官則在民。」此其乘除消長，理與事誠然也。而今之時，則亦有不然者。征求苛煩，十室九罄，殫竭民間之所有而歸之公上，謂宜盡在官也。然歲一不稔，南北之待哺者輒以饑聞，是猶可諉也，曰：「歲也。」至於金之所入，凶年不損，豐年不加，而亦有匱焉。太倉內帑之所儲積，日出而不給。又一切為救濟之術，而取盈於經制常額之外，以求足乎金，而卒未嘗足，何也？
translation_en:
…sages governing the realm could make beans and grain as abundant as water and fire, yet still valued them highly. Thus Chao Cuo’s statement that an enlightened ruler prizes the five grains and holds gold and jade cheap is indeed sound. Yet in our own time things are otherwise. Give gold to a child three feet tall, tossing it to him [?], and he smiles delightedly and cannot bear to let it go. The world’s love of gold is generally like this. As for the five grains, people sometimes regard them lightly. Why do they have no time to care about that on which life and death, fullness and hunger depend, yet so eagerly prize gold? Surely it is because they have uses for it. As expenditure of money grows more extravagant each day, those above and below exact ever more from one another. Grain becomes cheaper by the day, while money becomes increasingly scarce. This tendency must continue until both are exhausted.

Sima Guang said: “The wealth produced by Heaven and Earth amounts only to this fixed quantity; if it is not with the officials, it is with the people.” Such additions and subtractions, decreases and increases, are indeed true both in principle and in practice. Yet in our own time things are otherwise here too. Exactions are harsh and numerous; nine households in ten have been emptied. Everything the people possess is exhausted and handed over to the authorities, so one would suppose that it must all be in official hands. Yet whenever a year’s harvest fails, those awaiting sustenance in north and south immediately report hunger. This can still be explained away by saying, “It is the harvest.” But monetary receipts neither diminish in a bad year nor increase in a good one, and nevertheless there are shortages here too. The reserves accumulated in the Court of the Imperial Granaries and the palace treasury are paid out daily and do not suffice. Every expedient for relief is then employed, and additional sums are extracted beyond the regular statutory quotas in the hope of obtaining enough money. Yet in the end there is never enough. Why is this?

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
夫固有所耗之也耗之者無經而天地之
所生者有限歲復一歲將大虧而不可復
支其敝豈獨在民哉嗟夫天下如一身然
民其氣血也國腹心也氣血失所養而腹
心亦憊矣故今之歛財於下而上復空虛
者氣血腹心俱受病也爲今之計莫若先
圖足民欲求足民莫若先務除害二者因
乎其權與勢耳勢有損益而吾能酌之善
乘勢者也權有盈虛而吾能調之善達權
===
者也或者不此之察而惟損下益上日以
足國爲計是猶虞人惜裘之美反而負薪
其亦不知重本也又或不事節縮而務操
切以漁獵乎民俾盈者愈盈而虛者愈虛
是猶止沸者不即去薪其亦不知急要也
是故欲足民者其道有二欲除害者其道
亦有二何謂足民之道重農事也崇節儉
也語曰民者背本而趨末天下之大殘也
今之有田者苦于稅役迫於逋負輒貿易

亦有二何謂足民之道重農事也崇節儉
也語曰民者背本而趨末天下之大殘也
今之有田者苦于稅役迫於逋負糶貿易
punctuated:
夫固有所耗之也。耗之者無經，而天地之所生者有限，歲復一歲，將大虧而不可復支，其敝豈獨在民哉！嗟夫！天下如一身然，民其氣血也，國腹心也。氣血失所養，而腹心亦憊矣。故今之歛財於下而上復空虛者，氣血腹心俱受病也。爲今之計，莫若先圖足民；欲求足民，莫若先務除害。二者因乎其權與勢耳。勢有損益，而吾能酌之，善乘勢者也；權有盈虛，而吾能調之，善達權者也。
或者不此之察，而惟損下益上，日以足國爲計，是猶虞人惜裘之美，反而負薪，其亦不知重本也。又或不事節縮，而務操切以漁獵乎民，俾盈者愈盈而虛者愈虛，是猶止沸者不即去薪，其亦不知急要也。
是故欲足民者，其道有二；欲除害者，其道亦有二。何謂足民之道？重農事也，崇節儉也。語曰：「民者背本而趨末，天下之大殘也。」今之有田者，苦于稅役，迫於逋負，輒貿易
translation_en:
There must indeed be something draining these resources. Such depletion knows no bounds, whereas what Heaven and Earth produce is limited. Year after year, the deficit will grow until it can no longer be sustained. Will the resulting harm fall upon the people alone? Alas! All under Heaven is like a single body: the people are its vital energy and blood, and the state its abdomen and heart. When the vital energy and blood lack nourishment, the abdomen and heart also become exhausted. Thus, when wealth is now exacted from those below, yet those above remain empty-handed, both the vital energy and blood and the abdomen and heart suffer illness. The best course now is first to secure sufficiency for the people; to secure sufficiency for the people, the best course is first to eliminate what harms them. Both depend upon judicious adjustment and circumstances. Circumstances bring losses and gains: if we can weigh them, we are adept at taking advantage of circumstances. In exercising discretion there are surpluses and deficiencies: if we can balance them, we are adept at judicious adjustment.
Some fail to perceive this and merely diminish those below to enrich those above, constantly devising ways to provide enough for the state. This is like a forester who, cherishing the beauty of his fur coat, turns it inside out to carry firewood: he too fails to understand the importance of preserving the foundation. Others make no effort to curb expenditure, but concentrate on harsh exactions, hunting and fishing among the people for gain. They make those with a surplus ever richer and those with a deficiency ever poorer. This is like someone trying to stop water boiling without promptly removing the firewood: he too fails to understand what urgently needs doing.
Thus, there are two ways to secure sufficiency for the people, and there are likewise two ways to eliminate what harms them. What are the ways to secure sufficiency for the people? To give weight to agriculture and to esteem frugality. As the saying goes: “For the people to turn their backs on the root and pursue the branches is a great calamity for all under Heaven.” Nowadays, those who own fields, burdened by taxes and labor service and pressed by arrears and debts, readily sell them…

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
焉以少蘇旦夕而其稍有貯畜者則又輸
之以補官榮或事末作以趨利焉而田因
之以輕矣田輕則農病而莫之肯事也欲
粟有羨盈也何由乎於是而塞開納之路
禁游食之衆使民皆著於本轉而縁南畝
而又均其賦節其力無所擾之而專農事
則力本業給衣食比櫛崇墉民多私積而
各樂其所矣語曰淫侈之俗日以長天下
之大賊也今官榮末作之徒交勝而不已
===
無農夫之勞有阡陌之得遂粲然以競其
侈心而僭上踰制莫之究極欲金無傷耗
也可得乎於是而示之好尚立之表式令
室廬有制也服食有等也婚喪賓客小大
之禮各有節也則入於農者常有餘而經
於用者又無濫財用焉得而不裕風俗焉
得而不厚哉故勢日以趨下而民日以就
益百姓富而君不獨貧執事所謂上與下
兩利而俱足者是也何謂除害之道戒貪

punctuated:
焉，以少蘇旦夕，而其稍有貯畜者，則又輸之以補官榮，或事末作以趨利焉，而田因之以輕矣。田輕則農病，而莫之肯事也。欲粟有羨盈也，何由乎？於是而塞開納之路，禁游食之衆，使民皆著於本，轉而縁南畝，而又均其賦，節其力，無所擾之而專農事，則力本業，給衣食，比櫛崇墉，民多私積，而各樂其所矣。
語曰：「淫侈之俗日以長，天下之大賊也。」今官榮末作之徒交勝而不已，無農夫之勞，有阡陌之得，遂粲然以競其侈心，而僭上踰制，莫之究極。欲金無傷耗也，可得乎？於是而示之好尚，立之表式，令室廬有制也，服食有等也，婚喪賓客小大之禮各有節也，則入於農者常有餘，而經於用者又無濫，財用焉得而不裕，風俗焉得而不厚哉？故勢日以趨下，而民日以就益，百姓富而君不獨貧。執事所謂上與下兩利而俱足者，是也。
何謂除害之道？戒貪
translation_en:
…selling it to gain a little respite from one day to the next. Those who have accumulated some savings, meanwhile, pay them over to obtain official honors, or pursue secondary occupations for profit; thus farmland comes to be held in low esteem. When land is undervalued, agriculture suffers, and no one is willing to undertake it. How, then, can there be a surplus of grain? Accordingly, close off the avenues for obtaining office through contributions and prohibit people from living idly at others’ expense. Make all the people firmly attach themselves to the fundamental occupation and turn to cultivating the southern fields. Further, equalize their taxes, moderate demands upon their labor, and leave them undisturbed to devote themselves to agriculture. Then they will exert themselves in the fundamental occupation and have sufficient clothing and food. Grain will stand close as the teeth of a comb and high as walls; the people will have ample private stores, and each will be content with their lot.
As the saying goes, “Daily growth in habits of extravagance and luxury is a great scourge of the realm.” Today, those enjoying official honors and those pursuing secondary occupations endlessly vie to outdo one another. Without the farmer’s toil, they obtain the fields’ yield. They then compete in splendid displays of extravagance, presumptuously adopting the usages of their superiors and exceeding established limits, without any end to it. Can one expect wealth to escape depletion? Accordingly, show them what to esteem and establish models for them to follow. Let dwellings be subject to prescribed standards, clothing and food be differentiated by rank, and the rites of marriage, mourning, and receiving guests, great and small alike, each have their proper bounds. Then agricultural income will always leave a surplus, while expenditure will remain free from excess. How could financial resources fail to be abundant, and customs fail to become sound? Thus the force of circumstances will daily tend downward [?], while the people daily gain greater benefit. When the common people are wealthy, the ruler will not alone be poor. This is what you mean by both those above and those below benefiting and enjoying sufficiency.
What are the ways to eliminate harm? Guard against greed…

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
吏也哉諸冗也周官以六計弊羣吏之治
必以廉爲本故廉者吏之首善也今之爲
民牧者豈無尚貞履約愛民且自愛者乎
然而不如是者衆也挾其威與術以乗民
之弱且愚朘民之脂膏竊公之贏羨若谿
壑之深無厭也所謂盜臣與聚斂之臣或
且兼之矣於是而吏以賍敗者必按跡嚴
治之或逮治焉吏以廉稱者必褒嘉寵異
之且殊陟焉則不肖者有所奪其情而不
===
敢肆而賢者益相與以勵厥守矣周禮有
司徒以制賦之入又有職歲以制賦之出
故周之理財也理其出而已今貢賦有定
則而經用無常數以一歲之入較一歲之
出其不足常十之四而費之濫溢者復途
轍孔多窠臼糾集所謂官浮于冗員禄浮
于冗食兵浮于冗費盖實兼之矣于是而
綜核鉤稽之以究其鹵莽滲漏之弊刷洗
釐剔之以塞其磬蹙枵虚之原則浩穰之

punctuated:
吏也，哉諸冗也。周官以六計弊羣吏之治，必以廉爲本，故廉者，吏之首善也。今之爲民牧者，豈無尚貞履約、愛民且自愛者乎？然而不如是者衆也。挾其威與術，以乗民之弱且愚，朘民之脂膏，竊公之贏羨，若谿壑之深無厭也。所謂盜臣與聚斂之臣，或且兼之矣。於是而吏以賍敗者，必按跡嚴治之，或逮治焉；吏以廉稱者，必褒嘉寵異之，且殊陟焉。則不肖者有所奪其情而不敢肆，而賢者益相與以勵厥守矣。

周禮有司徒以制賦之入，又有職歲以制賦之出，故周之理財也，理其出而已。今貢賦有定則，而經用無常數，以一歲之入較一歲之出，其不足常十之四，而費之濫溢者復途轍孔多，窠臼糾集。所謂官浮于冗員，禄浮于冗食，兵浮于冗費，盖實兼之矣。于是而綜核鉤稽之，以究其鹵莽滲漏之弊；刷洗釐剔之，以塞其磬蹙枵虚之原，則浩穰之
translation_en:
…officials, and cutting back the various redundancies [?]. The Offices of Zhou assesses the administration of officials by six criteria, invariably taking integrity as their foundation. Integrity is therefore an official’s foremost virtue. Among those who now shepherd the people, are there none who esteem rectitude, practice restraint, love the people, and cherish their own good name? Yet those who do otherwise are numerous. Wielding their authority and their stratagems, they exploit the people’s weakness and ignorance, drain their lifeblood, and steal the surplus of public funds. Their appetite is as bottomless as a deep ravine. Some may indeed combine the qualities of what are called thieving ministers and ministers who exact excessive levies. Accordingly, officials disgraced by corruption must have their deeds investigated and be sternly punished, or be arrested for trial. Officials renowned for integrity must be commended, accorded special favor, and given exceptional promotion. Then the unworthy will have their impulses checked and will not dare act recklessly, while the worthy will increasingly encourage one another to remain steadfast in their principles.

In the Rites of Zhou, the Minister of Education regulates revenue from levies, while the Director of Annual Accounts regulates its expenditure. Thus Zhou’s management of finances consisted simply in managing expenditure. Today tribute and taxation follow fixed standards, but regular expenditure has no constant amount. Comparing one year’s receipts with one year’s expenditure, the shortfall is commonly four-tenths. Moreover, excessive expenditure flows through very many channels, and entrenched abuses are tangled together. What are called an official establishment swollen with supernumeraries, stipends swollen by those drawing unearned support, and military affairs swollen with unnecessary expenses are indeed all present together. Accordingly, comprehensive scrutiny and auditing must uncover the abuses of careless administration and financial leakage; thorough cleansing and rectification must block the sources of depletion, straitened resources, and empty coffers [?]. Then the vast…

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
用可漸給凋瘵之民可少蘇矣此則握其
權于上而酌盈以濟乎虛執事所謂去其
害穀與金者是也害除則利自興將穀與
金並饒而下與上同給矣是故足民之道
於下之損者益之其勢常在下也除害之
道於上之盈者虛之其權常在上也損益
者以穀爲先而金非所重也盈虛者以金
爲重而穀非所先也善乘其勢而握其權
則固互相須而交相濟也唐劉晏制萬物
===
低昂常操天下贏貲以佐軍興雖拏兵數
十年斂不及民而用度足第五琦當軍興
隨事趣辦人不益賦而國用豐是二人者
不取之民而財自足豈天雨鬼輸哉亦得
夫損益之宜盈虛之術而已矣頃者
皇上軫念民依肇修耕籍每春和則下佈種之
詔遇水旱則竭祈省之忱或
發帑輸粟或蠲稅免租所以勤恤乎農務者
何其至耶邇因軍需靡費度支告匱則自

…the provisioning of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and even the stores and military supplies along all the frontiers have been rigorously scrutinized; redundant personnel, from those in the administrative offices to the staff of the palace directorates, have all been reduced or dismissed. The annual savings truly amount to no less than several hundred thousand. How far-reaching, too, are these measures to economize on expenditure! With His Majesty’s virtuous intentions so clearly proclaimed and his benevolent favor so widely bestowed, the state ought to be wealthy and its public granaries well stocked, every household adequately supplied and every person provided for. Yet if one looks to the officials, they have no reserves; if one looks to the people, few have anything stored away. The plight of pulling at one’s lapels only to expose one’s elbows is often seen, and the distress of clipping the nails down into the flesh cannot be avoided. The reason for this can be discerned.

A transmitted text says: “The ruler orders all things on Heaven’s behalf; ministers carry out the ruler’s commands and convey them to the people.” Perhaps those charged with affairs are content with idle neglect, merely following established routines and inherited practices to discharge their obligations; intimidated by considerations of advantage and harm, they constantly look ahead and behind to keep themselves secure. Those who cling to rigid views, like someone playing a zither with its bridges glued in place, do not investigate ways to adapt to changing circumstances; those who fail to understand the duty of crossing a river together in the same boat do not put the state’s urgent needs first. Thus, vast though imperial beneficence is, some of it still fails to flow through, while some of the common people’s grievances still fail to reach those above. What can this be but the failure of the responsible officials to carry out His Majesty’s intentions fully? Thus, only when all the timbers are ready can the building of a house be accomplished; only when the five flavors are balanced can a properly seasoned broth be made. The Great Learning…

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
乎其不匱也有是具也而衆望歸之矣夫
節之立也由於已而具之施也存乎時時
而用也則達諸天下不者亦以善其身而
傳諸後是故趠然高蹈匪以釣竒也劃然
遠播匪以炫能也其節誠修其具誠在二
者備矣是謂全德衆望攸歸譽盛自致匪
飾行而要名也愚嘗執此以覽觀往昔品
隲名流盖自三五以降雖淳厚漸漓而光
岳之氣蜿嬗扶輿磅礴而鬱積者往往鍾
===
瑰偉之材發寥廓之士上下數千載間未
易以悉數也姑舉執事所詢者言之有處
巖穴之間負天下之望如段干木魯仲連
嚴光黃憲其人焉諸葛亮謝安才猷未試
之先亦四子之倫也有處廊廟之間負天
下之望如汲黯楊綰其人焉范仲淹司馬
光功烈未究之先亦二子之倫也夫干木
踰垣厲守文侯式其閭而東征之難息焉
仲連輕世肆志平原屈其辨而帝秦之議

punctuated:
乎其不匱也。有是具也，而衆望歸之矣。夫節之立也由於已，而具之施也存乎時。時而用也，則達諸天下；不者，亦以善其身而傳諸後。是故趠然高蹈，匪以釣竒也；劃然遠播，匪以炫能也。其節誠修，其具誠在，二者備矣，是謂全德。衆望攸歸，譽盛自致，匪飾行而要名也。愚嘗執此以覽觀往昔，品隲名流。盖自三五以降，雖淳厚漸漓，而光岳之氣蜿嬗扶輿，磅礴而鬱積者，往往鍾瑰偉之材，發寥廓之士。上下數千載間，未易以悉數也。

姑舉執事所詢者言之：有處巖穴之間，負天下之望，如段干木、魯仲連、嚴光、黃憲其人焉。諸葛亮、謝安才猷未試之先，亦四子之倫也。有處廊廟之間，負天下之望，如汲黯、楊綰其人焉。范仲淹、司馬光功烈未究之先，亦二子之倫也。夫干木踰垣厲守，文侯式其閭，而東征之難息焉。仲連輕世肆志，平原屈其辨，而帝秦之議
translation_en:
…ample and inexhaustible. Possessing such capacities, he becomes the focus of the expectations of all. Integrity is established through oneself, while the exercise of one's capacities depends upon the times. If the times permit one to enter service, one extends one's influence throughout the realm; otherwise, one cultivates one's own person and transmits one's example to posterity. Thus, rising loftily above the world is no means of courting a reputation for singularity, nor is the conspicuous spread of one's fame a means of flaunting one's abilities. When integrity is truly cultivated and capacities are truly present, both are complete: this is called perfect virtue. The expectations of all converge upon such a person, and great renown comes of itself; it is not a matter of embellishing one's conduct to seek a name. I have sought to apply this standard in surveying the past and appraising its eminent figures. Since the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, although simplicity and sincerity have gradually declined, the vital energies of the heavenly lights and earthly peaks, winding and unfolding, vast and densely accumulated [?], have often gathered to produce extraordinary talents and men of expansive spirit. Across several thousand years, they cannot readily be enumerated in full.

Let me speak, for the moment, of those about whom you have asked. Some dwelt among cliffs and caves yet bore the expectations of the whole realm: Duangan Mu, Lu Zhonglian, Yan Guang, and Huang Xian were such men. Zhuge Liang and Xie An, before their talents and plans had been put to the test, also belonged in the company of these four. Others occupied positions at court and bore the expectations of the whole realm: Ji An and Yang Wan were such men. Fan Zhongyan and Sima Guang, before their achievements had been fully realized, also belonged in the company of these two. Ganmu climbed over a wall to avoid an audience and steadfastly maintained his principles. Marquis Wen bowed against his carriage crossbar when passing Ganmu's neighborhood, and the threat of an eastward military expedition subsided. Zhonglian held worldly honors lightly and freely pursued his aspirations. The Lord of Pingyuan yielded to his eloquence, and the proposal to recognize Qin's ruler as emperor…

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
寢馬蟬蛻軒冕之外折衝尊俎之餘其遠
致足稱也嚴光高步潁陽寄跡一絲之釣
而節義所激漢鼎繫之黃憲潜修慎陽比
量千頃之陂而風旨所感士類慕之奪奸
雄覬覦之念消士友鄙吝之萌其高標可
想也之四子者耽長往之趣者也諸葛亮
抱膝隆中長吟梁父隱然有卧龍之譽焉
逮感知三顧遂奠鼎足之業謝安陶情山
水高謝塵寰蕭然有凌霞之致焉及出當
===
===
國柄竟貽典午之安管樂長材東山雅量
民不失望其在此乎汲黯詰張湯之刻斥
公孫之詐直氣勁節天子重之淮南異謀
有所憚而不發固無假於重權也其社稷
之臣歟楊綰居家不問生業祿廩悉分姻
舊清名儉德天下高之京兆騶從聞相命
而輒損固無俟於歲月也其縉紳之表歟
之二子者樹匡世之績者也范仲淹志抱
先憂而以天下為任進百官之圖縱西夏

translation_en:
…was laid to rest [?]. Shedding the trappings of official rank as a cicada sheds its shell, he turned back conflict over the ceremonial vessels of a banquet: his lofty aspirations deserve praise. Yan Guang strode above worldly concerns at Yingyang, lodging his life in fishing with a single thread; the integrity and righteousness he inspired helped sustain the Han dynasty. Huang Xian cultivated himself in seclusion at Shenyang, his capacity likened to a reservoir spanning a thousand qing; scholars admired him, moved by his character and ideals. One extinguished the covetous designs of ambitious schemers; the other dispelled the first stirrings of narrow-minded meanness among his fellow scholars. Their lofty example can well be imagined. These four men delighted in withdrawing from the world for good.

Zhuge Liang clasped his knees at Longzhong and chanted the Song of Liangfu, quietly acquiring the reputation of a “Sleeping Dragon.” Moved at last by the recognition shown him in three visits, he laid the foundations for a realm that stood as one leg of a tripod. Xie An nurtured his spirit among mountains and waters, loftily withdrawing from the dusty world, with an untrammelled bearing that seemed to rise above the clouds. When he emerged to take the reins of government, he ultimately secured peace for the Sima dynasty. With talents like those of Guan Zhong and Yue Yi, and the cultivated magnanimity of the recluse of Dongshan, they did not disappoint the people. Was this not where their distinction lay?

Ji An challenged Zhang Tang’s harshness and denounced Gongsun Hong’s deceit. The Son of Heaven esteemed his upright spirit and unyielding integrity. The prince of Huainan’s rebellious designs were held in check by fear of him and never put into action. He certainly had no need to rely on great power: was he not a true minister safeguarding the altars of soil and grain? Yang Wan paid no attention to earning a livelihood at home, distributing all his official stipend among relatives by marriage and old acquaintances. All under Heaven esteemed his unsullied reputation and frugal virtue. On hearing of his appointment as chief minister, the governor of Jingzhao immediately reduced his mounted attendants. There was certainly no need to wait months or years for his influence to take effect: was he not an exemplar for the official class? These two men established achievements in setting the world aright.

Fan Zhongyan cherished the resolve to be the first to feel concern and took responsibility for all under Heaven upon himself. He submitted a chart of the officials and released the Western Xia …

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
之旅康濟弘畧不待奉天章之對而才已
見矣司馬光學本不欺而以國家為念進
五劄之規持新法之諫軫民至意不待興
元祐之治而德已孚矣庶士承風田夫知
姓永世有辭其在此乎嗟乎出處異致心
迹殊觀稱毁殊情始終易態聚廬而居同
閈而處以某問某盖有曰吾不知之者矣
况身處巖穴而才猷未試者或垢俗以動
其槩或疵物以激其清而恒不免離羣之
身居廊廟而功業未究者或矯衆以伸
其志或急節以赴其會而恒不免狥世之
嫌久矣夫聞望之難也廼古之人令譽宣
昭無論遐邇久近莫不仰休光欽懿烈此
豈聲音笑貌率爾為之而僥倖其或得者
哉無亦耿介拔俗慷慨厲時其節與具有
大過人者耶今夫麟遊藪而仁氣揚鳳巢
阿而德輝著幾相為感也君子高世之節
猶是也不言而天下信之後世為準焉即

猶是也不言而天下信之後世爲準焉耶
punctuated:
之旅，康濟弘畧，不待奉天章之對而才已見矣。司馬光學本不欺，而以國家為念，進五劄之規，持新法之諫，軫民至意，不待興元祐之治而德已孚矣。庶士承風，田夫知姓，永世有辭，其在此乎？

嗟乎！出處異致，心迹殊觀，稱毁殊情，始終易態。聚廬而居，同閈而處，以某問某，盖有曰「吾不知之」者矣。况身處巖穴而才猷未試者，或垢俗以動其槩，或疵物以激其清，而恒不免離羣之；身居廊廟而功業未究者，或矯衆以伸其志，或急節以赴其會，而恒不免狥世之嫌。久矣夫，聞望之難也！廼古之人，令譽宣昭，無論遐邇久近，莫不仰休光，欽懿烈。此豈聲音笑貌，率爾為之，而僥倖其或得者哉？無亦耿介拔俗，慷慨厲時，其節與具有大過人者耶？

今夫麟遊藪而仁氣揚，鳳巢阿而德輝著，幾相為感也。君子高世之節猶是也，不言而天下信之，後世為準焉，即
translation_en:
…the troops of Western Xia [?]. His broad strategies for bringing peace and relief showed his ability even before he answered the imperial questions in the Tianzhang Pavilion. Sima Guang grounded his learning in refusing to deceive and kept the state foremost in his thoughts. He presented admonitions in five memoranda and persisted in remonstrating against the New Policies. His profound concern for the people had already won trust in his virtue before he brought about the good government of the Yuanyou era. Scholars followed their example, and farmers knew their names; praise of them endured through the ages. Was this not the reason?

Alas! Serving in office and living in retirement entail different aims; inward intentions and outward conduct present different aspects. Praise and blame arise from differing sentiments, and attitudes change from beginning to end. Even among people living in neighboring dwellings and sharing the same village gate, if one asks someone about another, there are surely those who say, “I do not know him.” How much more so with those who dwell in rocky retreats, their abilities and plans still untried! Some denounce vulgar customs to stir their own resolve; others find fault with the world to intensify their purity. Yet they constantly incur the charge of estranging themselves from others [the transcription appears incomplete here]. Those who occupy court office but have not yet brought their achievements to fruition may defy the multitude to fulfill their aspirations, or press forward urgently to seize an opportunity; yet they constantly incur suspicion of pandering to the world. How long it has been difficult to win renown and esteem!

Yet the fine reputations of the ancients shone forth conspicuously. Whether far or near, in their own time or long afterward, everyone looked up to their splendid radiance and revered their admirable deeds. Could this have been achieved through mere words, smiles, and appearances, casually assumed in the hope of some lucky success? Was it not rather that they stood upright above vulgar convention and roused their age with spirited resolve, possessing integrity and ability far beyond those of others?

Now, when the qilin roams the marshland, an influence of benevolence spreads; when the phoenix nests upon a hill, the radiance of virtue becomes manifest. Subtle impulses evoke a response in one another. Such, too, is the gentleman’s integrity, which rises above his age: without speaking, he wins the trust of all under Heaven, and later generations take him as their standard. Even…

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
身之顯晦弗論已今夫水懷珠而川媚石
韞玉而山輝實不容掩也君子經世之具
猶是也未行而天下信之後世為準焉即
位之崇卑弗論已嚴光諸人所以負天下
之望者節也而未始無其具仲淹諸人所
以負天下之望者具也而未始不修其節
向使砥礪亢矣而不閑於具則索之易窮
名奚取焉若殷浩是已弱冠馳聲清徽卓
越通人伺其去就蒼生卜其安危可不謂
===
名乎而束之高閣之言足稱達識由其具
之不豫也才畧具矣而不植其節則迫之
易玩功且勿貴焉若韓信是已秉鉞東麾三
秦底定卷旆北指燕趙風靡可不謂功乎
而易與之侮切中生平由其節之不立也
甚哉名與功之不足恃而高世之節經世
之具所宜豫養而兼全者也則干木以下
諸君子者是已雖然干木仲連抗節亂世
貞矣要其指歸不合□於大道謝安矯情鎮

punctuated:
身之顯晦弗論已。今夫水懷珠而川媚，石韞玉而山輝，實不容掩也。君子經世之具猶是也，未行而天下信之，後世為準焉，即位之崇卑弗論已。嚴光諸人所以負天下之望者，節也，而未始無其具；仲淹諸人所以負天下之望者，具也，而未始不修其節。向使砥礪亢矣，而不閑於具，則索之易窮，名奚取焉？若殷浩是已。弱冠馳聲，清徽卓越，通人伺其去就，蒼生卜其安危，可不謂名乎？而「束之高閣」之言，足稱達識，由其具之不豫也。才畧具矣，而不植其節，則迫之易玩，功且勿貴焉。若韓信是已。秉鉞東麾，三秦底定；卷旆北指，燕趙風靡，可不謂功乎？而「易與」之侮，切中生平，由其節之不立也。
甚哉，名與功之不足恃，而高世之節、經世之具，所宜豫養而兼全者也！則干木以下諸君子者是已。雖然，干木、仲連抗節亂世，貞矣，要其指歸，不合□於大道。謝安矯情鎮
translation_en:
…whether he himself is prominent or obscure need not be discussed. Now, when water holds pearls, the river becomes beautiful; when rocks contain jade, the mountain shines. What is substantial cannot be concealed. So too with the gentleman’s capacities for ordering the world: even before he puts them into practice, all under Heaven trust him, and later generations take him as their standard. The eminence or lowliness of his position need not be discussed.
What enabled Yan Guang and men like him to command the expectations of all under Heaven was their integrity; yet they were never without practical capacities. What enabled Fan Zhongyan and men like him to command those expectations was their practical capacities; yet they never failed to cultivate their integrity. Suppose a man has disciplined himself to lofty heights but lacks proficiency in practical affairs: put him to the test, and his resources are soon exhausted. What value, then, has his reputation? Yin Hao was such a man. Already renowned at twenty, he possessed an exceptionally pure reputation. Discerning men watched whether he would enter office or withdraw, and the common people looked to him for signs of their own security or peril. Could this not be called fame? Yet the remark that he should be “put away on a high shelf” deserves to be called perceptive, for he had not prepared himself with the requisite capacities.
If a man possesses talent and strategic ability but has not established his integrity, he is easily manipulated when pressed, and even his achievements deserve no esteem. Han Xin was such a man. Wielding the battle-axe of command, he directed his forces eastward and pacified the Three Qin; furling his banners and heading north, he made Yan and Zhao yield like grass before the wind. Could these not be called achievements? Yet the contemptuous description of him as “easy to deal with” struck at the very heart of his life, for his integrity had not been firmly established.
How utterly insufficient it is to rely upon fame and achievement! Integrity that rises above the world and capacities for ordering the world must be cultivated in advance and brought to perfection together. Ganmu and the other gentlemen mentioned exemplify this. Nevertheless, although Ganmu and Zhonglian upheld their integrity in a disordered age and remained steadfast, when their ultimate aims are examined, they did not accord [?] with the Great Way. Xie An restrained his feelings to steady…

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
物談虛崇侈君子不由也若嚴子陵之逸
致黃叔度之宏宇汲長孺之切直楊公權
之廉操諸葛孔明之大畧范希文司馬君
實之純德殆庶幾乎九原可作也愚誠願
為執鞭欣慕之焉然而非其極也執事謂
古人必有可法者其惟伊尹乎躬耒耜而
樂堯舜也而世不以為迂湯始以幣聘之
囂囂而不顧也而世不以為伉已而就湯
而世不以為徇翊商受命纘服有夏而世
===
不以為異彼所以取信於天下者何其豫
耶應龍潜於深淵靈幻倏爍人覩其神而
莫測也及騰馳雲霧上下天地變化風雨
滋育萬類人被其利而莫知也蓋自一介
取予推之千駟萬鍾非道義而不屑也高
世之節孰尚焉然而非有心於潔已也自
匹夫匹婦耻不被堯舜之澤而左右厥辟
以式于九圍也經世之具孰周焉然而非
有意於趨時也是故專美有商高視千古

物談虛崇侈君子不由也若嚴子陵之逃
致黃叔度之宏宇汲長孺之切直楊公權
之廉操諸葛孔明之大畧范希文司馬君
實之純德殆庶幾乎九原可作也愚誠願
爲執鞭欣慕之焉然而非其極也執事謂
古人必有可法者其惟伊尹乎躬耒耜而
樂堯舜也而世不以爲迂湯始以幣聘之
囂囂而不顧也而世不以爲伉已而就湯
而世不以爲狗翊商受命纘服有夏而世
===
不以爲異彼所以取信於天下者何其豫
耶應龍潛於深淵靈幻倏爍人覩其神而
莫測也及騰馳雲霧上下天地變化風雨
滋育萬類人被其利而莫知也蓋自一介
取予推之千駟萬鍾非道義而不屑也高
世之節孰尚焉然而非有心於潔已也自
匹夫匹婦不被堯舜之澤而左右厥辟
以式于九圍也經世之具孰周焉然而非
有意於趨時也是故專美有商高視千古
punctuated: 物，談虛崇侈，君子不由也。若嚴子陵之逸致、黃叔度之宏宇、汲長孺之切直、楊公權之廉操、諸葛孔明之大畧、范希文、司馬君實之純德，殆庶幾乎！九原可作也，愚誠願為執鞭，欣慕之焉。然而非其極也。執事謂古人必有可法者，其惟伊尹乎？躬耒耜而樂堯舜也，而世不以為迂；湯始以幣聘之，囂囂而不顧也，而世不以為伉；已而就湯，而世不以為徇；翊商受命，纘服有夏，而世不以為異。彼所以取信於天下者，何其豫耶！應龍潜於深淵，靈幻倏爍，人覩其神而莫測也；及騰馳雲霧，上下天地，變化風雨，滋育萬類，人被其利而莫知也。蓋自一介取予，推之千駟萬鍾，非道義而不屑也，高世之節孰尚焉？然而非有心於潔已也。自匹夫匹婦耻不被堯舜之澤，而左右厥辟，以式于九圍也，經世之具孰周焉？然而非有意於趨時也。是故專美有商，高視千古
translation_en: …others; discoursing on emptiness and exalting extravagance are not paths the gentleman follows. As for Yan Ziling’s lofty detachment, Huang Shudu’s breadth of spirit, Ji Changru’s earnest frankness, Yang Gongquan’s incorruptible conduct, Zhuge Kongming’s grand strategic ability, and the pure virtue of Fan Xiwen and Sima Junshi—these perhaps come close to the ideal! If they could rise from their graves, I would sincerely wish to hold their whips as an attendant, so gladly do I admire them. Yet even these do not represent the utmost attainment. You suggest that among the ancients there must be someone worthy of emulation: would that not be Yi Yin? He personally worked the plow and delighted in the Way of Yao and Shun, yet the world did not regard him as impractical. When Tang first sought his service with gifts, he remained self-possessed and paid no heed, yet the world did not regard him as arrogant. Later he entered Tang’s service, yet the world did not regard him as accommodating himself to another’s wishes. He assisted Shang in receiving Heaven’s Mandate and succeeding to Xia’s rule, yet the world did not regard this as improper. How far in advance he had laid the foundations of the trust he commanded throughout the realm! When the winged dragon lies hidden in the deep abyss, its numinous transformations flash forth: people behold its divine power but cannot fathom it. When it races through clouds and mist, ascending and descending between heaven and earth, transforming wind and rain and nourishing all living things, people receive its benefits without understanding their source. From the giving or taking of the smallest thing to accepting a thousand teams of four horses or ten thousand measures of grain, Yi Yin disdained anything inconsistent with the Way and righteousness. Who could surpass his integrity, which rose above the world? Yet he had no deliberate intention of keeping himself unsullied. Ashamed if even one ordinary man or woman failed to receive the blessings of Yao and Shun, he assisted his sovereign in bringing order to the nine regions. Whose capacities for ordering the world were more complete? Yet he had no deliberate intention of courting the opportunities of his age. Thus he alone enjoyed such renown under Shang, standing exalted above the ages…

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
迄今莫與爭功而較名者允也其元聖哉
儒者有言寧學聖人而未至不欲以一善
而成名且志伊之訓愚生夙聞之矣執事
幸勿以為狂
第五問
楊州民
同考試官都給事中梁批安攘乃
國家大計此策洞悉時弊區畫有方真經濟之才也錄之
同考試官編修呂批南北練兵正今時急務
子能究極利弊斟酌時宜皆鑿鑿可措諸行事
稱為俊傑非耶
考試官學士董批此問反覆探究專重練兵
乃發策之始意也諸作多綴浮詞而闇于本指
子獨能慷慨發憤悉陳遠猷其志于用世者矣
考試官大學士袁批練兵之於調兵利害奚啻
什伯今南北當事者類以調兵為一時之計糜
財毒民甚矣子獨條析練兵之利不可以裨
廟堂之石畫耶
===

punctuated:
迄今莫與爭功而較名者，允也，其元聖哉！儒者有言：「寧學聖人而未至，不欲以一善而成名。」且志伊之訓，愚生夙聞之矣。執事幸勿以為狂。

第五問
楊州民

同考試官都給事中梁批：「安攘乃國家大計，此策洞悉時弊，區畫有方，真經濟之才也，錄之。」

同考試官編修呂批：「南北練兵，正今時急務。子能究極利弊，斟酌時宜，皆鑿鑿可措諸行事。稱為俊傑，非耶？」

考試官學士董批：「此問反覆探究，專重練兵，乃發策之始意也。諸作多綴浮詞而闇于本指，子獨能慷慨發憤，悉陳遠猷，其志于用世者矣。」

考試官大學士袁批：「練兵之於調兵，利害奚啻什伯！今南北當事者，類以調兵為一時之計，糜財毒民甚矣。子獨條析練兵之利，不可以裨廟堂之石畫耶？」

…down to the present, none has rivaled his achievements or matched his renown. Truly, was he not the supreme sage! A Confucian scholar has said: “I would rather study to become a sage and fall short than win renown for a single virtue.” Moreover, I, your humble student, have long heard the teaching that one should aspire to emulate Yi Yin. May you, honored sir, not deem me presumptuous.

Fifth Policy Question
Yang Zhoumin

Comment by Associate Examiner Liang, Chief Supervising Secretary: “Securing peace within and repelling threats from without are great matters of state. This policy essay thoroughly understands the failings of the times and proposes well-conceived measures. Here is a true talent for statecraft. Select it.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Lü, Compiler: “Training troops in both north and south is precisely the urgent task of the present day. You have thoroughly investigated the advantages and disadvantages and weighed what suits the circumstances of the times. Your proposals are all definite and practicable. Would it not be right to call you an outstanding talent?”

Comment by Examiner Dong, Academician: “This question probes the matter repeatedly, placing particular emphasis on training troops: that was the original intention in setting it. Most submissions string together empty phrases while remaining ignorant of its essential purport. You alone have expressed impassioned resolve and fully set forth far-reaching plans. You are surely one who aspires to serve the world.”

Comment by Examiner Yuan, Grand Secretary: “In weighing advantages and disadvantages, training troops is more than ten or a hundred times better than transferring troops! Those now responsible for affairs in both north and south generally resort to transferring troops as a temporary expedient, grievously wasting resources and afflicting the people. You alone have analyzed point by point the benefits of training troops. Could this not assist the court in framing firm plans?”

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
執事策諸生而欲求濟世之畧體國之忠
也故以時務終焉今時之務在西北則患
虜宣大薊鎮最急在東南則患寇首難浙
直轉入閩廣頃且薄江右矣古稱極治莫
過唐虞而猾夏之防奸宄之慮猶自不免
庸何損於聖世乎第今之建議者不審其
要而煩言以飾聽圖事者不核其實而虚
文以飾觀則嘗竊疑之矣何謂要南北之
練兵是也何謂實知練兵要矣力去其弊
===
而嚴責其成是也夫薊鎮宣大密邇
畿輔頻年數數告警膻幕内逼疆事日增武
備寝弛戎行半耗即隷於籍者率多選懔
無復勇悍沉鷙漁陽突騎之風乃鍛甲砥
劔矯箭累弦未能創敵而未見休時故曰
最急也往者督臣議設垣墻墩堡議大城
京後将重險而預防一勞而永逸也因以復
大寧之戍奠開平之都讋諸夷之心息四
郊之燧其見卓矣然而塹山堙谷嫌於絶

練兵是也何謂實知練兵要矣力去其弊
===
而嚴責其成是也夫薊鎮宣大密邇
畿輔頻年數告警𤠣奔內馳擾事曰增武
備寖弛戍行半耗即隸於籍者率多選愞
無復勇悍沉鷙漁陽突騎之風乃鍜甲砥
鋒矯箭累弦未能創敵而未見休時故曰
最急也往者督臣議設垣墻墩堡議大城
京後將重險而預防一勞而永逸也因以復
大寧之戍奠開平之都讋諸夷之心息四
郊之燧其見卓矣然而塹山堙谷爍於絕
punctuated:
執事策諸生，而欲求濟世之畧、體國之忠也，故以時務終焉。今時之務，在西北則患虜，宣大、薊鎮最急；在東南則患寇，首難浙直，轉入閩廣，頃且薄江右矣。古稱極治，莫過唐虞，而猾夏之防、奸宄之慮，猶自不免，庸何損於聖世乎？第今之建議者，不審其要，而煩言以飾聽；圖事者，不核其實，而虚文以飾觀，則嘗竊疑之矣。何謂要？南北之練兵是也。何謂實？知練兵要矣，力去其弊，而嚴責其成是也。
夫薊鎮、宣大密邇畿輔，頻年數數告警，膻幕内逼，疆事日增，武備寝弛，戎行半耗。即隷於籍者，率多選懔，無復勇悍沉鷙、漁陽突騎之風。乃鍛甲砥劔，矯箭累弦，未能創敵，而未見休時，故曰最急也。往者督臣議設垣墻墩堡，議大城京後，将重險而預防，一勞而永逸也。因以復大寧之戍，奠開平之都，讋諸夷之心，息四郊之燧，其見卓矣。然而塹山堙谷，嫌於絶
translation_en:
You, honored examiners, put policy questions to the candidates to seek strategies for aiding the age and loyalty that takes the state's interests to heart; hence you conclude with current affairs. Among today's concerns, in the northwest the threat comes from the northern invaders, with Xuanfu, Datong, and the Ji garrison in the greatest urgency. In the southeast the threat comes from marauders: the troubles began in Zhejiang and the Southern Metropolitan Region, spread into Fujian and Guangdong, and recently have even approached Jiangxi. Since antiquity, no age has been reckoned better governed than those of Tang Yao and Yu Shun. Yet even they could not avoid guarding against those who disturbed the Chinese realm or worrying about evildoers within and without. How, then, could such troubles detract from a sage-governed age? What I have privately questioned is simply this: those who advance proposals today fail to discern what is essential and embellish their speeches with prolix arguments, while those who undertake affairs fail to examine practical realities and put on an impressive display of empty formalities. What is essential? Training troops in both north and south. What constitutes practical substance? Once the importance of training troops is understood, vigorously eliminating its abuses and strictly demanding results.
The Ji garrison, Xuanfu, and Datong lie close to the capital region. In recent years they have repeatedly sounded alarms. The rank-smelling tents of the northern invaders press inward; frontier troubles increase daily, military preparedness steadily slackens, and the ranks have been depleted by half. Even those still on the rolls are mostly timid [?], with none of the fierce courage and resolute ferocity once characteristic of Yuyang's charging cavalry. Armor is forged, swords sharpened, arrows straightened, and bowstrings fitted; yet the enemy remains unwounded, and no respite is in sight. That is why I call this the most urgent concern.
Previously, the supreme commander proposed constructing walls, watchtowers, and forts, and building extensive fortifications behind the capital, intending to multiply defensive barriers and forestall danger—to expend effort once and secure lasting peace. Thereby he would restore the garrison at Daning, secure the capital at Kaiping, strike fear into the hearts of the various foreign peoples, and extinguish the alarm beacons on every side. His vision was outstanding. Yet cutting trenches through mountains and filling valleys risks severing …

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
地畫境分圻能無棄野異日者叩垣登陴
恐貽與共之戚矣矧物力方虛閭左復發
豈節民之道耶又儒臣議於幽冀之域土
著之民一切賦役咸與蠲貸惟飼馬而供
稅列屯而置隊也因以固疆圉之守施寬
假之恩張制禦之威成拱翼之勢其見遠
矣然而籍民爲兵近於保甲月操歲閱能
不妨時異日者揭竿挺鋤恐貽腹心之患
矣矧公計方殷輸將悉罷豈裕國之謨耶
===
是故兩議者皆非要也夫宣大急矣猶爲
外戶也若薊鎮則堂奧也東起山海西抵
居庸延袤幾二千里而近膺筦鑰之司者
懷震驚之慮胡可不審其要哉遠徴延固
近檄宣遼在我仰給於客兵在彼寔疲於
遠戍戎心洊啓滋蔓難圖于役靡遑及瓜
莫代甲胄苦於蟣虱杼軸竭於轉輸非乆
遠之畫也經畧之臣謂宜先拊循三衛詗
彼虛實絕彼鄉導以夷攻夷至善策也夫

punctuated:
地，畫境分圻，能無棄野？異日者叩垣登陴，恐貽與共之戚矣。矧物力方虛，閭左復發，豈節民之道耶？又儒臣議於幽冀之域，土著之民，一切賦役咸與蠲貸，惟飼馬而供稅，列屯而置隊也。因以固疆圉之守，施寬假之恩，張制禦之威，成拱翼之勢，其見遠矣。然而籍民爲兵，近於保甲，月操歲閱，能不妨時？異日者揭竿挺鋤，恐貽腹心之患矣。矧公計方殷，輸將悉罷，豈裕國之謨耶？
是故兩議者皆非要也。夫宣大急矣，猶爲外戶也；若薊鎮，則堂奧也。東起山海，西抵居庸，延袤幾二千里，而近膺筦鑰之司者，懷震驚之慮，胡可不審其要哉？遠徴延固，近檄宣遼，在我仰給於客兵，在彼寔疲於遠戍。戎心洊啓，滋蔓難圖；于役靡遑，及瓜莫代。甲胄苦於蟣虱，杼軸竭於轉輸，非乆遠之畫也。經畧之臣謂宜先拊循三衛，詗彼虛實，絕彼鄉導，以夷攻夷，至善策也。夫
translation_en:
…land. By drawing boundaries and dividing the territory, can we avoid abandoning the countryside? If one day the enemy strikes the walls and mounts the parapets, I fear we shall leave behind the distress of sharing them with the enemy [?]. Moreover, material resources are already depleted, yet the poorer households are again being levied for service. Is this a way to conserve the people's strength?
Civil officials have also proposed that all taxes and labor obligations of the settled inhabitants of You and Ji be remitted or deferred, requiring them only to rear horses in payment of their taxes, and organizing them into military settlements and units. This would strengthen frontier defenses, extend the benevolence of leniency, display the might of military control, and establish a protective formation around the capital. Their vision is far-reaching indeed. Yet registering civilians as soldiers resembles the baojia system of household organization. With monthly drills and annual inspections, could it fail to interfere with the agricultural seasons? If one day they raise poles and brandish hoes in rebellion, I fear this would leave a danger at the very heart of the realm. Moreover, when public financial needs are pressing, would abolishing all deliveries of revenue be a plan for enriching the state?
Thus neither proposal addresses the essential issue. The situation in Xuanfu and Datong is urgent, but they are still the outer doorway. Jizhen, by contrast, is the innermost chamber. Extending from Shanhaiguan in the east to Juyongguan in the west, it stretches nearly two thousand li. Those charged with guarding these nearby gateways harbor fears of alarming incursions: how could we fail to examine what is essential here? Troops are summoned from distant Yansui and Guyuan, and orders dispatched to nearer Xuanfu and Liaodong. We depend on troops brought in from elsewhere, while they are exhausted by distant garrison service. Hostile ambitions repeatedly arise, spreading until they become difficult to deal with. Those on service have no respite; even when their term expires, no replacements arrive. Men in armor suffer from lice and their eggs, while the resources of the looms are exhausted by transport and provisioning. This is no enduring plan.
The officials responsible for strategic planning say that we should first conciliate the Three Guards, ascertain their strengths and weaknesses, cut off their access to local guides, and use barbarians to attack barbarians. This is an excellent strategy. Now, …

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
拊循者惠也而懾服之者威也威振矣而
惠施焉而後弗敢玩也所以振其威者惟
練兵之爲要乎至於東南之事亦有然者
曩倭夷窺釁海島乘軍吏之弗戒潜竄浙
直間羣不逞之徒投機煽搆閩廣江右之
交多阨塞之墟萑苻之藪入焉嘯聚出焉
剽劫如迅飈如突豕隨撲而輒起少熄而
復熾州縣或窘於城守之未備村堡多潰
於壁野之未堅亦既急矣當事者戒心於
===
擊目之危而困智於徒手之搏於是議調
遣議召募搶攘紛紜莫知所出今劇寇固
在也重以千里被水患往往赤子爲蜴蛇
而作使爲狙詐勦捕之期胡可緩也問其
所以勦捕之者匪調即募耳豈其廢郡縣
之兵而乏鄉鄙之民耶西漢時郡國有材
官騎士太守都尉令長丞尉會都試課殿
最水處爲樓船邊郡行障塞有司以羽檄
徵發各因其地此郡縣之兵之實也彼役

punctuated: 拊循者，惠也；而懾服之者，威也。威振矣，而惠施焉，而後弗敢玩也。所以振其威者，惟練兵之爲要乎？至於東南之事，亦有然者。曩倭夷窺釁海島，乘軍吏之弗戒，潜竄浙直間。羣不逞之徒，投機煽搆。閩廣江右之交，多阨塞之墟、萑苻之藪，入焉嘯聚，出焉剽劫，如迅飈，如突豕，隨撲而輒起，少熄而復熾。州縣或窘於城守之未備，村堡多潰於壁野之未堅，亦既急矣。當事者戒心於擊目之危，而困智於徒手之搏，於是議調遣，議召募，搶攘紛紜，莫知所出。今劇寇固在也，重以千里被水患，往往赤子爲蜴蛇，而作使爲狙詐，勦捕之期胡可緩也？問其所以勦捕之者，匪調即募耳。豈其廢郡縣之兵，而乏鄉鄙之民耶？西漢時，郡國有材官、騎士，太守、都尉、令、長、丞、尉會都試，課殿最。水處爲樓船，邊郡行障塞，有司以羽檄徵發，各因其地，此郡縣之兵之實也。彼役
translation_en:
…To conciliate them is to show benevolence; to overawe them into submission is to exercise might. Only after might has been displayed and benevolence then bestowed will they dare not treat us lightly. Is not training troops the essential means of displaying that might?

The situation in the southeast is similar. Previously, the Japanese raiders watched from the offshore islands for an opening and, taking advantage of the military officers’ lack of vigilance, slipped into Zhejiang and the Southern Metropolitan Region. Bands of malcontents seized the opportunity to foment disorder. Where Fujian, Guangdong, and Jiangxi meet, there are many places of difficult terrain and marshy refuges for bandits. They enter these to gather their bands and emerge to plunder, like a violent gale or a charging boar. As soon as they are suppressed, they rise again; scarcely has the fire subsided before it blazes anew. Some prefectures and counties are hard pressed because their city defenses are unprepared; many fortified villages fall because their defenses of walls and countryside are insecure [?]. The situation has indeed become urgent. Those responsible are alarmed by the danger before their eyes, yet exhaust their ingenuity in fighting barehanded. They therefore debate troop transfers and recruitment, amid tumult and confusion, without knowing what course to take.

The formidable bandits are still present, and now flooding has afflicted a thousand li of territory besides. Again and again, the common people turn into lizards and snakes, and those who set them in motion practice cunning deception [?]. How can the campaign to suppress and capture them be delayed? Yet if one asks how they are to be suppressed and captured, the answer is merely either transferring troops or recruiting them. Are we then to abandon the troops of the prefectures and counties and exhaust the people of the countryside?

Under the Western Han, the commanderies and kingdoms maintained trained infantry and cavalry. Grand Administrators, Chief Commandants, Magistrates, Chiefs, Vice Magistrates, and Commandants assembled for the general military review and assessed the best and worst performances. In regions with waterways, the troops served aboard tower ships; in frontier commanderies, they patrolled fortified outposts. The responsible officials called them up with feathered dispatches, adapting their service to the locality. Such was the substance of the local military system. Those who serve…

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
於官而食於民見謂爲兵者非少也胡不
以漢制律之也唐李抱真守懷州遍籍人
戶三丁擇一給以弓矢曹偶習射歲終大
校第能否示賞責二年皆爲精兵此鄉鄙
之民爲兵之效也彼民猶夫故也胡不以
抱真之法施之也夫寇始發而調且募也
猶可委也今數載於茲矣三年爲國遂使
知方七年教民可俾即戎賢聖所作爲可
不深思而勉効之乎應調之兵非我族類
===
惟思干賞而蹈利應募之兵率多無藉豈
能安制而矜節縱橫睥睨僵良善以爲已
功稍逆其意則羣起譟呼比遣之歸則四
分鹵掠視薊鎮調兵之害爲尤甚矣乃泄
泄焉玩志於蓄艾之圖託言於采薇之役
獨何心哉是故南北勢殊而練兵爲要一
也愚跧伏草野竊聞
聖天子明燭萬里而心周乎四海屢屢
詔旨切責督撫諸臣念此至熟也諸臣圖方略
alt_text:
於官而食於民見謂爲兵者非少也胡不
以漢制律之也唐李抱真守懷州遍籍人
戶三丁擇二給以弓矢曹偶習射歲終大

猶可委也今數載於茲矣三年爲國遠使
知方七年教民可俾即戎賢聖所作爲可
不深思而勉效之乎應調之兵非我族類
===
惟恩干賞而蹈利應募之兵率多無藉豈
能安制而矜節縱橫睥睨僵良善以爲己
功稍逆其意則羣起譟呼北遣之歸則四
分鹵掠覬覦鎮調兵之害爲尤甚矣乃泄
泄焉玩志於蒿艾之圖託言於采薇之役
獨何心哉是故南北勢殊而練兵爲要一
也愚跧伏草野竊聞
聖天子明燭萬里而心周乎四海屢厪
詔旨切責督撫諸臣念此至熟也諸臣圖方略
punctuated:
於官而食於民，見謂爲兵者非少也，胡不以漢制律之也？唐李抱真守懷州，遍籍人戶，三丁擇一，給以弓矢，曹偶習射，歲終大校，第能否，示賞責，二年皆爲精兵。此鄉鄙之民爲兵之效也。彼民猶夫故也，胡不以抱真之法施之也？夫寇始發而調且募也，猶可委也；今數載於茲矣。三年爲國，遂使知方；七年教民，可俾即戎。賢聖所作爲，可不深思而勉効之乎？應調之兵，非我族類，惟思干賞而蹈利；應募之兵，率多無藉，豈能安制而矜節？縱橫睥睨，僵良善以爲已功；稍逆其意，則羣起譟呼；比遣之歸，則四分鹵掠，視薊鎮調兵之害爲尤甚矣。乃泄泄焉，玩志於蓄艾之圖，託言於采薇之役，獨何心哉？是故南北勢殊，而練兵爲要一也。
愚跧伏草野，竊聞聖天子明燭萬里，而心周乎四海，屢屢詔旨切責督撫諸臣，念此至熟也。諸臣圖方略
translation_en:
…serve the authorities and are fed by the people: those presently called soldiers are by no means few. Why not regulate them according to the Han system? When Li Baozhen governed Huaizhou under the Tang, he registered all households, selected one out of every three adult males, supplied them with bows and arrows, and grouped them together to practice archery. At the end of the year he held a general review, graded their abilities, and announced rewards and reprimands. Within two years, all had become seasoned soldiers. This demonstrates the effectiveness of turning the rural population into soldiers. The people are still as they were before; why not apply Baozhen’s methods to them? When the bandits first arose, reliance on troop transfers and recruitment might still have been excusable. But several years have now passed. Three years of governing a state could bring its people to understand the proper course; seven years of teaching the people could fit them for warfare. Should we not ponder deeply what the worthies and sages accomplished and strive to emulate them?
The troops brought in by transfer are not of our own people and think only of seeking rewards and pursuing gain. Those recruited are mostly men without standing; how can they abide by discipline and prize integrity? They swagger about arrogantly, killing innocent people and claiming this as their own achievement. If their wishes are crossed in the slightest, they rise together in uproar; when sent home, they scatter in all directions to plunder. The harm they cause is even worse than that caused by troops transferred from the Jizhen garrison command. Yet officials remain complacent, neglecting plans to lay up mugwort for future treatment and making excuses about the burdens of military service evoked in “Gathering Bracken.” What can they be thinking? Thus, although conditions in the north and south differ, the essential importance of training troops is the same.
I, in my ignorance, live obscurely in the countryside. I have humbly heard that the sagely Son of Heaven’s insight illuminates ten thousand li and his concern embraces all within the four seas. His repeated edicts sternly reprimanding the supreme commanders, grand coordinators, and other officials show how thoroughly he has considered this matter. The officials devise strategies…

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
奉奔走而厥效未覩毋乃去弊而責成者
不核其實耶夫練兵於北將帥事也練兵
於南守令事也制之以督撫監之以憲臣
請
上之賞罰而鼓舞其下之心志者也自練兵之
議行以殊能顯績而蒙不次之賞以無能
僨事而加不測之罰者誰耶有之而弗能
辨愚也匿焉而弗以聞罔也其咎有攸歸
矣古者推轂閫外則閫外之事聽其便宜
===
今之待將帥者輕矣有投石超距之士而
無以優之有鞭扑貫耳之法而不敢施之
柰何欲結其心而作其氣也古者保障一
方則一方之賦聽其出入今之待守令者
輕矣有父兄子弟之懷而無以恤之有身
臂指使之勢而無以制之柰何欲習其教
而遂其志也夫使將帥守令而不可任也
則是不擇而用之者之過也既擇其可用
之才而怯其得為之具所謂縶騏驥之足
alt_text:
奉命奔走而厭效未覩毋乃去弊而責成者
不核其實耶夫練兵於北將帥事也練兵
於南守令事也制之以督撫監之以憲臣

辨悉也匿焉而弗以聞罔也其咎有攸歸
矣古者推轂閫外則閫外之事聽其便宜
===
今之待將帥者輕矣有投石超距之士而
無以優之有鞭扶貫耳之法而不敢施之
柰何欲結其心而作其氣也古者保障一
方則一方之賦聽其出入今之待守令者
輕矣有父兄子弟之懷而無以恤之有身
臂指使之勢而無以制之柰何欲習其教
而遂其志也夫使將帥守令而不可任也
則是不擇而用之者之過也既擇其可用
之才而怯其得爲之具所謂縶騏驥之足
punctuated:
奉奔走，而厥效未覩，毋乃去弊而責成者不核其實耶？夫練兵於北，將帥事也；練兵於南，守令事也。制之以督撫，監之以憲臣，請上之賞罰，而鼓舞其下之心志者也。自練兵之議行，以殊能顯績而蒙不次之賞，以無能僨事而加不測之罰者，誰耶？有之而弗能辨，愚也；匿焉而弗以聞，罔也。其咎有攸歸矣。
古者推轂閫外，則閫外之事聽其便宜。今之待將帥者輕矣，有投石超距之士而無以優之，有鞭扑貫耳之法而不敢施之，柰何欲結其心而作其氣也？古者保障一方，則一方之賦聽其出入。今之待守令者輕矣，有父兄子弟之懷而無以恤之，有身臂指使之勢而無以制之，柰何欲習其教而遂其志也？夫使將帥守令而不可任也，則是不擇而用之者之過也。既擇其可用之才，而怯其得為之具，所謂縶騏驥之足
translation_en:
…carry out their duties with all dispatch, yet results have not been seen. Might this not be because those charged with eliminating abuses and demanding results fail to examine the actual circumstances? Training troops in the north is the responsibility of military commanders; training troops in the south is the responsibility of prefects and county magistrates. Supreme commanders and grand coordinators are to direct them, and censorial officials to supervise them, requesting rewards and punishments from His Majesty to stir the resolve of their subordinates. Since the proposal to train troops was put into effect, who has received rewards outside the normal order for exceptional ability and outstanding achievements, or extraordinary punishment for incompetence and the ruin of affairs? If such cases exist but officials cannot distinguish them, that is folly; if they conceal them and fail to report them, that is deception. The blame has its proper objects.
In antiquity, when a commander was sent forth beyond the threshold, affairs beyond that threshold were left to his discretion. Today, military commanders are accorded little weight. They have men capable of throwing stones and leaping great distances, yet lack the means to reward them generously; they have disciplinary measures of flogging and piercing the ears, yet dare not apply them. How, then, can they hope to win their men's hearts and rouse their spirit? In antiquity, those charged with protecting a region were allowed discretion over the receipt and expenditure of its tax revenues. Today, prefects and county magistrates are accorded little weight. They cherish their people as fathers and elder brothers cherish sons and younger brothers, yet lack the means to care for them. Their position should enable them to command as the body directs the arms and fingers, yet they lack the means to exercise control. How, then, can they hope to have their training practiced and their purposes fulfilled? If military commanders, prefects, and county magistrates cannot be entrusted with responsibility, the fault lies with those who employ them without proper selection. Once men of serviceable talent have been selected, however, to shrink from giving them the means to act [?] is what is called fettering the feet of a thoroughbred…

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
絏孟賁之手者也是故賞罰嚴於上事權
重於下而後核實之令可行也夫核實者
練兵之要也其在於北調兵漸掣不必言
矣而主兵之練也必稽影射革占役禁挑
選復逋逃務期充伍而足用焉若邊墻工
役卒歲勤勞文吏詰查經時漁擾生計朘
於公費口食縮於私求凡此致弊之端實
去之可也其在於南官兵宜訓不必言矣
而鄉兵之練也必覈里甲明部隊招逃匿
===
時巡行務俾適均而各守焉若繫名公府
遂煩應役委權胥吏緣以為奸農業廢於
蒐田家殖棄於調遣凡此致弊之端實去
之可也夫北地禦虜火器最捷而東南制
寇短兵為宜武經載火攻之篇光弼創礟
飛之制晁錯條服習之利唐宗耀劒舞之
長皆核實以濟用者也今將帥亦知火器
之捷也每當閱視傭工以應已而置之矣
守令演武莫不肅隊而趨持矛而舞佯呼

絏孟賁之手者也。是故賞罰嚴於上，事權重於下，而後核實之令可行也。夫核實者，練兵之要也。其在於北，調兵漸掣，不必言矣。而主兵之練也，必稽影射，革占役，禁挑選，復逋逃，務期充伍而足用焉。若邊墻工役，卒歲勤勞；文吏詰查，經時漁擾；生計朘於公費，口食縮於私求：凡此致弊之端，實去之可也。其在於南，官兵宜訓，不必言矣。而鄉兵之練也，必覈里甲，明部隊，招逃匿，時巡行，務俾適均而各守焉。若繫名公府，遂煩應役；委權胥吏，緣以為奸；農業廢於蒐田，家殖棄於調遣：凡此致弊之端，實去之可也。
夫北地禦虜，火器最捷，而東南制寇，短兵為宜。《武經》載火攻之篇，光弼創礟飛之制，晁錯條服習之利，唐宗耀劒舞之長，皆核實以濟用者也。今將帥亦知火器之捷也，每當閱視，傭工以應，已而置之矣。守令演武，莫不肅隊而趨，持矛而舞，佯呼
translation_en:
…and bind the hands of Meng Ben. Thus, only when rewards and punishments are rigorously administered above and substantial authority over affairs is vested below can orders to verify actual conditions be carried out. Such verification is essential to training troops. In the north, it goes without saying that troops transferred in should gradually be withdrawn. But in training the local garrison troops, one must investigate fraudulent registration, abolish their appropriation for labor service, prohibit selective transfers, and bring back deserters, striving to fill the ranks and make them adequate for service. As for labor on the frontier walls that keeps them toiling throughout the year; investigations by civil officials that subject them to prolonged extortion and harassment; livelihoods depleted by public expenses and food allowances diminished by private exactions—all these sources of abuse must actually be eliminated. In the south, it goes without saying that government troops should be trained. But in training the local militia, one must scrutinize the lijia household organization, clearly define units, recall those who have fled or gone into hiding, and conduct periodic inspection tours, ensuring that burdens are properly and evenly apportioned and that each man guards his assigned place. If registration with government offices merely burdens them with labor service; if authority entrusted to clerks affords opportunities for wrongdoing; if farming is neglected because of hunting musters and household livelihoods are abandoned because of troop deployments—all these sources of abuse must actually be eliminated.
For resisting the northern foes, firearms are most effective, while for subduing bandits in the southeast, weapons for close combat are appropriate. The Military Classics contain a chapter on attack by fire; Guangbi devised a system of hurling projectiles [?]; Chao Cuo enumerated the advantages of practiced familiarity; and the Tang emperor displayed excellence in sword dancing. All these grounded practical effectiveness in actual proficiency. Today, commanders also know the effectiveness of firearms, yet whenever an inspection takes place, they hire workmen to meet its demands and afterward set the weapons aside. When prefects and magistrates conduct military drills, they invariably have their men advance in orderly ranks, brandish spears in a dance, and give feigned shouts…

translation_en:
…shouting in a crowd, as though putting on entertainment—what benefit could this possibly bring in practice? Thus, only through wholehearted training can their skills become refined and prove effective in use. Yet even this is not enough. You wish to hear an argument that probes fully to the root of the matter. Foolish and blunt as I am, may I finish setting out my views? Training troops at the Ji garrison has failed to produce results because the officials shrink from vigorous action and prefer to carry on as before. They rely on troops brought in from elsewhere for defense, while slighting the local troops and employing them as laborers. Day and night, their hearts are set on obtaining transfers and shedding their burdens. The southeast is a source of fiscal revenue, and military operations entail enormous expense. Without troop transfers and recruitment, these officials would have no means to exercise their talents for embezzlement and satisfy their appetite, as bottomless as a ravine. Alas! If they do not sincerely serve the interests of the state, but seek their own private convenience, on what can the state depend?
Our sovereign is sagely and wise. His recent punishment of frontier commanders for their lack of martial prowess displayed his great authority. His dispatch of ministry officials to provide military supplies in the north, and his edict reducing taxes in the southeast, displayed his great benevolence. This is the moment for loyal ministers and men of resolve to devote their determination and utmost strength, even sacrificing their lives, to repay the state. If the Ji garrison is prepared, troops from Yan, Gu, Xuan, and Liao need not be transferred, and the northwest will thereby enjoy peace. If affairs in the southeast are also managed appropriately, all under Heaven will be secure and free from anxiety. Thus, responding to changing circumstances as opportunities arise, and devising appropriate measures according to local conditions, is the responsibility of those…

計三秦賈誼料諸侯王其言卒驗若持左

引此三人者發其端固以俊傑望諸生諸

translation_en: …is the responsibility of those charged with affairs. In the Warring States period, Su Qin devised a strategy for the Six States; under the Han, Han Xin planned the conquest of the Three Qin, and Jia Yi assessed the feudatory kings. Their predictions were ultimately borne out, as surely as presenting the left half of a contract to claim what was owed. You, honored Examiner, lament that impractical scholars fail to understand the needs of the times, and have cited these three men to introduce the subject, surely hoping to find outstanding talent among us candidates. I am merely a callow student of textual exegesis: how could I merit your discerning inquiry? I have ventured to set down what I have heard, for your consideration and selection.

translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Metropolitan Examination

In the forty-first year of Jiajing (1562), it was time to hold the Metropolitan Examination for scholars from throughout the realm. Before this, His Majesty had selected his servant Ne 訥 as Minister of Rites, while his servants Gong 拱 and Sheng 陞 were appointed simultaneously as Left and Right Vice Ministers, respectively. These appointments were evidently made in preparation for the Metropolitan Examination. Subsequently, the ministry requested the appointment of officials to preside over the examination. His Majesty specially commissioned his servants Wei 煒, Grand Secretary, and Fen 份, Academician, to undertake this duty.

At that time, Wei was attending and assisting His Majesty morning and evening, never leaving his side. Yet, because of the importance attached to the examination, His Majesty sent him. On the day they were to enter the examination compound, they respectfully proceeded to Yinghe Gate, kowtowed, and took their leave. His Majesty specially dispatched gifts of gold insignia and scarlet robes, wine, and food. I, your servant Fen, also undeservedly shared in …

translation_en:
…in these gifts. This was indeed extraordinary favor, an exceptional distinction without precedent. Your servant privately reflects that his abilities are utterly unworthy; yet, fortunately, Your Majesty has accepted and promoted him, nurturing him with a bounty comparable to that of Heaven and Earth. Twice before I presided over the examination, and on both occasions received generous gifts. Now I have again been entrusted with this weighty charge and received still more generous gifts—favor to which my limited abilities cannot possibly do justice. I can only exert myself eagerly, hoping to find worthy men and thereby repay some small part of it.
At this time, palace construction happened to be under way. On that day, all the officials crowded along the road in attendance, rejoicing and exulting. I ought to have accompanied them, but was occupied with my official duties. From within the examination compound, I could only gaze toward its auspicious emanations and behold its…

text:
祥光屬天北向稱慶而九日士
初試之日也古以士為梁棟
易言棟隆吉而其時不先不
後適與之合夫事固有先而
期固有兆意士將有如兹棟
者以出而應其時乎臣聞匠
氏貴于得木典試者貴于得
===

得之而萬木皆後矣士而有
如棟者國之榦也典試者得
之而羣材皆下矣臣甚為諸
士願而臣伏觀我

punctuated: 祥光屬天，北向稱慶。而九日，士初試之日也。古以士為梁棟，《易》言「棟隆吉」，而其時不先不後，適與之合。夫事固有先，而期固有兆，意士將有如兹棟者，以出而應其時乎？臣聞匠氏貴于得木，典試者貴于得士。木而有棟，室之榦也；匠氏得之，而萬木皆後矣。士而有如棟者，國之榦也；典試者得之，而羣材皆下矣。臣甚為諸士願。而臣伏觀我皇上睿智天縱，總攬萬機，端拱九重，明照四海，人臣方奔走
translation_en: …its auspicious radiance reaching heaven, I faced north and offered congratulations. Now the ninth was the day of the candidates’ first examination session. In antiquity, scholars were regarded as beams and ridgepoles. The Book of Changes says, “The ridgepole rises: auspicious.” The timing, neither earlier nor later, coincided precisely with this. Events surely have their antecedents, and appointed times their portents. Might there emerge among these scholars men like this ridgepole, ready to answer the needs of their time? Your servant has heard that what matters to a master carpenter is obtaining timber, and what matters to those presiding over examinations is obtaining scholars. Among timbers, the ridgepole is the mainstay of a house; once the master carpenter obtains it, all other timbers take second place. Among scholars, a man who resembles a ridgepole is the mainstay of the state; once those presiding over examinations obtain him, all other talents rank below him. Your servant earnestly wishes this for the candidates. And your servant humbly observes that our Emperor, endowed by Heaven with sagacity and wisdom, takes charge of the myriad affairs of government. Seated with hands folded within the ninefold palace, his discernment illuminates all within the four seas, while his ministers are busily hastening about…

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:

清光而况耆賢翼戴俊彦在列
治化方隆豈後進之士復能裨
補萬一而輒望以為國之榦
則以大海雖充而天下之水
畢歸者各聚其流也太倉雖

皇上御極以来凡舉會試者十四
矣而于此尤軫
聖心至親為加念夫
聖皇之心一動則

宫殿之役

不暇，何敢仰望清光？而况耆賢翼戴，俊彦在列，治化方隆，豈後進之士復能裨補萬一，而輒望以為國之榦？則以大海雖充，而天下之水畢歸者，各聚其流也；太倉雖足，而天下之貢畢至者，各率其職也。
自皇上御極以来，凡舉會試者十四矣，而于此尤軫聖心，至親為加念。夫聖皇之心一動，則百神效職，萬靈供事，即如宫殿之役
translation_en:
…with no time to spare, how could they dare to gaze upward upon Your Majesty’s radiant presence? Moreover, venerable worthies support the throne, and outstanding men stand in the ranks of office. Your transforming governance is flourishing: how could men newly entering service contribute even the slightest assistance, and yet presume to hope to become pillars of the state? It is because, though the great sea is full, all the waters under Heaven still flow into it, each gathering its own current; and though the imperial granaries are amply stocked, tribute from all under Heaven still arrives, each contributor fulfilling his duty.
Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, the Metropolitan Examination has been held fourteen times. Yet this occasion has especially engaged Your sagely concern, to the point that You have personally bestowed additional attention upon it. Once the sagely sovereign’s mind is moved, the hundred gods discharge their duties and the myriad spirits render service—as in the work on the palace buildings…

不顧欂顧而不專以其材之

往而見匠氏左引繩右引墨

矣其直而堅者雖小必收否
者雖大弗錄以其大而無當

===
大者爲櫟小者爲桷桷收而
不顧櫟顧而不專以其材之
未大也臣私識之異日者又
往而見匠氏左引繩右引墨
木之從直而中堅者無不收
矣其直而堅者雖小必收否
者雖大弗錄以其大而無當
punctuated:
天人協贊，上下闓懌，億萬年無疆之基，不日成矣。士號有知者，獨無激發以自效于國者乎？臣固于是而卜之矣。

雖然，願竊有言焉。曩臣嘗往閲工所，見匠氏者左援規，右援矩，木之中尺度者，無不收矣。大者為欂，小者為桷。桷收而不顧，欂顧而不專，以其材之未大也。臣私識之。異日者，又往而見匠氏左引繩，右引墨，木之從直而中堅者，無不收矣。其直而堅者，雖小必收；否者，雖大弗錄，以其大而無當
translation_en:
… Heaven and humanity lend their aid together, and those above and below rejoice. A foundation enduring without limit for countless ages will soon be completed. Can it be that among scholars, who are reputed to possess understanding, none will be stirred to offer their service to the state? Your servant has certainly taken this as a sign of what is to come.

Nevertheless, I would venture to say something further. Previously, I went to inspect the worksite and saw the craftsmen holding compasses in their left hands and squares in their right. They accepted every piece of timber that met the required dimensions. The larger pieces served as bracket timbers, and the smaller as rafters. The rafters were accepted but received no further attention; the bracket timbers received attention, but not exclusively, because their timber was not yet large enough [?]. I privately took note of this. On another day I went again and saw the craftsmen drawing out the measuring cord with their left hands and the ink line with their right. They accepted every piece of timber that was straight along its length and sound at its core. Those that were straight and sound were invariably accepted, however small; those that were not were rejected, however large, because, though large, they were unsuitable …

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
于用也臣又私識之既而臣
悟士者貴于取材而尤先于
立本夫砥節礪行貞士之所
以成信也秉德持操賢臣之
所以致身也古之人立德不
在大而慎行不在小芳芷不
以無人而不芳其性壹也楩
===
楠不以易地而不長其質定
也故利不能回所以淬志也
勢不能怵所以明守也立而
不搖所以飭範也行而不疑
所以約趨也木必培其根而
士必樹其本如使士而若此
則雖未用于

則雖未用于
punctuated: 于用也。臣又私識之。既而臣悟：士者貴于取材，而尤先于立本。夫砥節礪行，貞士之所以成信也；秉德持操，賢臣之所以致身也。古之人立德不在大，而慎行不在小。芳芷不以無人而不芳，其性壹也；楩楠不以易地而不長，其質定也。故利不能回，所以淬志也；勢不能怵，所以明守也；立而不搖，所以飭範也；行而不疑，所以約趨也。木必培其根，而士必樹其本。如使士而若此，則雖未用于
translation_en: …for use. Your servant again privately took note of this. Then I realized: in considering scholars, selecting talent is important, but establishing their moral foundations must come first. Tempering integrity and refining conduct are how upright scholars establish their trustworthiness; upholding virtue and maintaining moral resolve are how worthy ministers dedicate themselves to service. The ancients did not depend on great deeds to establish virtue, nor did they consider any act too small to merit care. Fragrant angelica does not cease to be fragrant because no one is present: its nature is constant. Pian and nan trees do not cease to grow when transplanted: their inherent qualities are fixed. Thus, remaining unswayed by profit is how scholars temper their resolve; remaining unintimidated by power is how they make clear the principles they uphold. Standing firm without wavering is how they put their exemplary conduct in order; acting without hesitation is how they discipline their course. Trees must have their roots nurtured, and scholars must establish their moral foundations. If scholars were like this, then even though they had not yet been employed in…

title: 嘉靖四十一年會試錄
text:
國其幹具矣如其不然而
國何賴焉又何取于材之有夫
竭精發憤思以効忠士之夙
心也遇
主逢時期以自見士之所大幸也
端本正始務以植躬義之所
先也得則進而光佐
===

世所戒始于毫釐辨以千里
士亦其自審哉臣既仰奉
上命其品第諸士公也非臣之所
得私也其于諸士相儆之語
亦公也非臣之所得私也錄
成用敢述其語以聞之于

成用敢述其語以聞之于
punctuated:
國，其幹具矣。如其不然，而國何賴焉？又何取于材之有？夫竭精發憤，思以効忠，士之夙心也；遇主逢時，期以自見，士之所大幸也；端本正始，務以植躬，義之所先也。得則進而光佐聖朝，顯策勳業，名垂後来；失則為世所戒。始于毫釐，辨以千里，士亦其自審哉！

臣既仰奉上命，其品第諸士，公也，非臣之所得私也；其于諸士相儆之語，亦公也，非臣之所得私也。錄成，用敢述其語以聞之于
translation_en:
…the state, he already possesses the capacity to serve it. If this is not so, on what can the state rely? And what use is there in possessing talent? To devote all one's energies and exert oneself, seeking thereby to render loyal service, is the scholar's longstanding aspiration. To encounter a ruler and meet with a favorable age, hoping thereby to show one's abilities, is the scholar's greatest good fortune. To rectify the foundation and set the beginning aright, striving thereby to establish one's moral character, is what righteousness puts first. If he succeeds in this, he advances to lend glorious assistance to the sagely dynasty, has his meritorious achievements illustriously recorded, and leaves his name to posterity; if he fails, he becomes a warning to the world. What begins as a difference of a hair's breadth diverges by a thousand li. Scholars should surely examine themselves!

Having reverently received His Majesty's command, I grade and rank these scholars impartially; this is not something in which I may indulge private preferences. The words of mutual admonition addressed to these scholars are likewise impartial; here too I may not indulge private preferences.
